info.title: Porelo Planner
info.description: Serves a project's planning board - its workflow, stories and issues kept in Git - to the Porelo window on the same computer. No call carries the planner's token. Every call but the proof is signed in its Porelo-Signature header with an HMAC-SHA256 under the token's UTF-8 bytes; a request without one valid signature, with two, or with an Authorization header answers 401 with an empty body, and so does one whose body is larger than 267264 bytes, the longest title and body GitHub takes with their JSON, 1048576 bytes for POST /projects/{project}/stories and /projects/{project}/issues, or 1052672 bytes for POST /projects/{project}/tasks/{task}/result. The signature is `porelo-planner-request-1;t=<time>;n=<nonce>;s=<hmac>`: the UTC time in seconds in decimal, no leading zero, at most 60 s off the planner's clock; 16 random bytes as nonce, each taken once; the HMAC over the ASCII label porelo-planner-request-1 and one zero byte, then each of these fields as its length in four bytes, big endian, and its bytes - the method, the raw request target as sent (the path and, when there is one, `?` and the raw query), the Host header, the Content-Type header (empty when absent), the SHA-256 of the body as sent (of no bytes when absent), the time as in the header and the nonce. Nonce and HMAC are base64url without padding, in their one canonical form. Every answer to a signed request but its 401 carries `Porelo-Answer: porelo-planner-answer-1;s=<hmac>`, the HMAC under the token over the label porelo-planner-answer-1 and one zero byte, then as length-prefixed fields the request's nonce, the status in decimal and the SHA-256 of the answer's body; the opening of the changes stream carries it with an empty field in place of the body's digest, and its events are not part of it. Before its first call, and again after a connection error, a timeout, a stream it opens again, a 401 or a change of the address file, a caller asks POST /proof that the planner on the port holds the token, and calls nothing when the answer is not the proof. A call that fails on a fault the planner answers by no other name answers 500 with the problem `urn:porelo-planner:Unexpected` and fixed words, the same for every such fault; the planner's log names the cause.

post.x-mcp: false the proof of the token, asked before any signed call
post.summary: Proof of the token
post.description: Proves that the planner listening on this port holds the token, without a signature and before anything of the person's is sent: the proof is the HMAC-SHA256 under the token's UTF-8 bytes over the ASCII label porelo-planner-proof-1, one zero byte, the port the planner listens on as two bytes, big endian, and the 32 challenge bytes, in base64url without padding. Only POST on the raw path /proof, without a query, is exempt from the signature. The body is application/json of at most 128 bytes, an object with exactly the one member challenge; anything else answers 400 with an empty body, and no refused proof is logged.

200.description: The proof.

400.description: The body is not one canonical challenge; the body is empty.

200.description: The planner serves calls.

post.x-mcp: false the mock mode, for the window's tests
post.summary: Restore the mock board
post.description: Only in the mock mode (`porelo-planner --mock`), for the window's tests: forgets every project given with the moves saved into its own copy of the mock board, so a project given again is served the mock board at `mock@1` and each test starts alike. Outside the mock mode a POST here answers 404, as for a path that does not exist.

204.description: The mock board is as it was at the start.

404.description: The planner does not run in the mock mode.

post.x-mcp: false the mock mode, for the window's tests
post.summary: Offer a reviewer on the mock board
post.description: Only in the mock mode (`porelo-planner --mock`), for the window's tests: gives the project a run whose pushed work waits at its author's gate push, with a reviewer offered there, as the planner's own flow makes it on the mock board as first served. The project's work then holds that run alone, in place of any run it held, and its `starts` the reviewer, by its role's name and parts and with the gate push as its place; the mock board itself is left as it is, and a reset forgets the run. Outside the mock mode a POST here answers 404, as for a path that does not exist.

204.description: The project's work holds the reviewer offered.

404.description: The planner does not run in the mock mode, or the project was not given.

post.x-mcp: false the mock mode, for the window's tests
post.summary: Hold a save on the mock board
post.description: Only in the mock mode (`porelo-planner --mock`), for the window's tests: gives the project one held save of the window's own, which its board's `heldSaves` then carries: it would change the priority of an issue of the mock board, and was tried three times, the last held with the forge's answer and its request id. A resend writes it as written whole and a drop removes it, each writing nothing to the mock board; a reset forgets it. Outside the mock mode a POST here answers 404, as for a path that does not exist.

204.description: The project's board carries the held save.

404.description: The planner does not run in the mock mode, or the project was not given.

put.x-mcp: false the window names the repository of a project it opens
put.description: Makes the project known with its own repository and branch; the same body again changes nothing. Another body retires the project first and drops its clones as the new one opens, so a failed call leaves the project unknown.

204.description: The project is known with this repository and branch.

get.description: Answers the project's states, phases, sound work rules, the faults found reading its workflow and board, and where its stories and issues are kept.

200.description: The project's workflow at the given revision.

get.x-mcp: false the changes stream, which the window follows
get.description: Streams the project's board as Server-Sent Events: event `board`, its `id` the board's revision and its `data` one `Board` object, first on each connection as implicit frame 0. Each later changed answer is event `change`, its `id` the new revision and its `data` one `BoardDelta`, taken against the last answer sent on this connection. Work-only changes retain the revision, including a cancellation or Needs you. Saves, polls and `refresh` publish the current board and work snapshot. An identical answer sends no event. A comment line `: keep-alive` comes every 15 s while nothing changes; a reader that falls behind gets one delta covering every skipped frame. Only sent board changes count as frames; load events and comments do not count. A reconnect, with `Last-Event-ID` or without, gets the current whole board first. An unknown project is refused before the stream starts. While the store reads the board, whole or by a look, event `load` tells the read's progress at least every 5 s, its `data` `{"state": "reading", "since", "read", "total", "lastRead", "from", "kind", "waitsFor"}`. `kind` is `whole` (also when it is absent) for a read of the whole board, item by item, a `refresh` told so from the moment it is asked, even while it waits behind a look; or `look` for a look at the board's item list for what changed since the board held, whose `read` counts the items its list showed so far and whose `total` is the larger of the items the board holds and those listed so far. `waitsFor` is `save` while the read told waits for the project a save or comment of the planner holds, and absent otherwise. A reader ignores a `kind` or `waitsFor` it does not know: an unknown `kind` counts as `whole`, an unknown `waitsFor` as absent. A read ends with its `board` or `change`, with `load` `{"state": "done"}` when it changed nothing, or with `load` `{"state": "failed", "problem", "failure", "parameters"}`: before the first board this ends the stream, after it the stream stays and the board held stands. A local project's kept directory the planner can no longer use fails its read with problem ItemsDirectoryRefused, `failure` its phrase and `parameters` naming the directory as that refusal does, only when it is an ItemsDirectory; no board is read meanwhile, from the default directory neither.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The last event id the window saw; the current board comes first in any case.

200.description: The stream's first board data is a `Board`; subsequent change data is a `BoardDelta`; load data tells read progress.

post.summary: Read the repositories now
post.description: Reads the project at once instead of waiting for the next poll. For a project kept in Git, the repositories are fetched and a new revision reaches every stream of the project before this call answers; a repository whose save is still pending is not fetched: it stands as the planner's own clone holds it until the save is pushed. For a tracked project, it answers at once, before its first board too, and the read's board follows on the stream, with `load` events while the read runs and a failed `load` when it fails.

200.description: The revision after the fetch for a project kept in Git; the revision held when the read began for a tracked project, null while it holds no board yet.

get.description: Answers a page of the project's stories with all their issues, without descriptions. State and priority select the story's own fields; repository selects a story when any of its issues is of that repository. Values within a filter are alternatives; different filters must all match. The open counts cover the whole board on every page. Follow next until null, keeping the same filters. The revision identifies store content; live work status may change between pages. Pages contain at most 60,000 JSON characters including their envelope, except an indivisible item larger than that bound, which is answered alone.

200.description: The stories at the given revision, without their descriptions.

post.summary: Make a story with new issues, or from issues that stand
post.description: Makes a story in the project's own repository in one of two ways, told apart by the body's members. A StoryRequest saves an idea a person, or an agent acting for them, wrote without a discussion: one story in the workflow's first state and an issue in that state in each repository the idea names, in one save, as a discussion's reported idea is saved; it changes no item that stands, so its `seen` may be empty and is not checked. The idea is checked against the idea format before anything is saved, and a malformed idea makes nothing (IdeaRefused). A save that stops after a part of it stands answers PartlySaved, naming the repositories that hold their part; a run whose story is gone is dropped first, so the new story never takes it over. A StoryFromIssuesRequest makes a story over issues that stand on the board: each must be an open issue of the workflow and no sub-issue of another issue, and is refused otherwise, each refused id named in the IdeaRefused answer. An issue another story holds leaves that story in the same save, as setStoryIssues moves it, and the story it leaves stays, if need be without issues, while an issue another story holds only under Also needs in its body is refused, since this call never changes that body; an issue a started task works, or one of its sub-issues, refuses the call (WorkRunning) and nothing is made. The issues become the story's issues in the order named and keep their own fields, and the story's state follows theirs. Every issue named is a target: it is checked against the version `seen` holds for it, read again from the tracker where the store keeps one, before anything is written; an issue changed since is ItemChanged, one without a version BasisIncomplete, and one hung under another parent there is IssueInStory, with nothing made. The story's body ends in a hidden HTML comment marking the request, a digest of its title, gain, test and the issues named. A save that stops after the story was made answers PartlySaved; after reading the board again, the same story and issues sent with the versions the new board shows, the story the earlier attempt made among them, finish it: the story carrying that request's mark, made by the same person within a day and holding no issue but those named, is taken, never made twice, an issue it already holds is not linked again, and it keeps the priority it holds. A story a person made, or one another request made, is never taken. A store that makes no story from issues that stand, such as the Git store, answers NotOffered before the body is checked. A run whose story is gone is dropped once the new story stands, so a refused call leaves the work record as it was; a gone story's run with a task still at work refuses the call, as does a started task that works one of the issues named or a sub-issue of one (WorkRunning, naming that issue). A StoryRequest JSON body is at most 1048576 bytes; a StoryFromIssuesRequest body is at most 65536 bytes. The changes stream announces the new board as it does after any save.

201.description: The story is saved, with its issues.

get.description: Answers one story with its issues and its description. An id two stories share answers NoSuchStory, since no one story is meant.

200.description: The story at the given revision.

get.description: Answers exactly the issues of one story.

200.description: The story's issues at the given revision.

put.description: Writes the story's whole issue list, in its order, checked against the versions `seen` holds for the story and for every issue hung in or taken out, whose parent changes: an issue taken out is no longer the story's, an issue hung in becomes the story's, and the order is the one sent. Each issue is named once and is one of the board's; an issue that is a sub-issue of another issue is refused (EditNotAllowed). An issue hung in that another story holds moves: it leaves that story's list and joins this one in the same save, all or none, both stories checked against the versions `seen` holds for them; on GitHub the sub-issue moves from one parent to the other, and the story it leaves stays, if need be without issues. An issue another story holds only under Also needs in its body is refused, since this call never changes that body. A list is refused (EditNotAllowed) for a story the board shows only in part, since a list written whole would drop the issue not shown, and a list that hangs in or takes out an issue a warning holds back; one kept in the list may be reordered. An issue a started task works, or one of its sub-issues, is not taken out (WorkRunning). On GitHub an issue becomes the story's sub-issue, and one the story's body names under Also needs keeps its place after the sub-issues and is not taken out by this call. A list equal to the story's saves nothing and answers the current revision. The JSON body is at most 65536 bytes. The changes stream announces the new board as it does after any save.

200.description: The list is saved, or was the story's already.

put.summary: Set a story's title and text
put.description: Writes the story's title and its parts What a user gains and The test, every other byte of its text as it was. A member left out stays as it is; null removes the part with its lead, and the title is never removed. Also needs (the story's issues, set through its issues), a person's own headings and the fields are not written by this call; a member naming them is refused (EditNotAllowed), and a body naming nothing is refused. The member labels sets the item's topic labels (TopicLabels): a label outside them that the item carries stays, and a name outside them is refused (LabelNotAllowed) before anything is written. The Git store sets no labels (NotOffered). On GitHub the item is read back after the write, since GitHub drops labels without an error for an account that may not set them; labels it carries other than every label sent - the topic labels asked and those of the person's own it carried - are refused (LabelsNotKept, naming the repository and the item), never answered as saved, while what else the edit wrote stands and the changes stream announces it. GitHub matches a label's name in any case, so a label it carries as Tests is the topic label tests: it counts as carried, is taken off when left out, and is never sent beside tests. A topic label the repository lacks is created by GitHub for the write in its own grey without a description and stays so: the next Refresh shows it as differing in the repository's warning, whose Labels correction sets it right. A text and labels equal to the item's save nothing and answer the current revision. The edit is checked against the version `seen` holds for the item, and on GitHub the item is read again right before the write and the edit refused (ItemChanged, naming the item) when a person changed it since; GitHub takes no condition on an issue's update, so a change made in the one round trip between that read and the write is overwritten, and stays in GitHub's own history of the item. A part whose text holds a line Markdown reads as a heading of the first or second level, a lead of another leading part, a blank line in a leading part, a code block, an HTML comment, a pre or a details block left open, or a text that would grow the body past the 65536 characters GitHub takes, is refused (EditNotAllowed) before anything is written; so is a body whose sections cannot be told apart for certain, with the first thing to repair. The JSON body is at most 267264 bytes. The changes stream announces the new board as it does after any save.

200.description: The text is saved, or held it already.

post.x-mcp: false offers a task that only the window starts, with the person
post.summary: Offer a task that discusses an idea
post.description: Answers one task for Porelo's Start that discusses an idea with the person: kind discussion, no role, no repository, no issues, mode AGENT, and as agent and model the first agent and model of the first sound work rule whose names are 1 to 128 UTF-16 code units, as defaults the person may change; it names no result file. The window starts it with every repository of the project read only, passing the offer as Start's callerKey. The task reports its idea back once through Porelo's Report, with the kind idea and as its text the idea as one JSON object in the idea format the brief carries, at most 65536 characters; this needs Porelo's settings to allow reports (limits.reports at least 1) and Report among the task's methods (mcp.methods), and a task without them reports nothing. The planner records only the offer: it reads the reports of the task Porelo recorded with that callerKey, every minute while a window follows the project, and saves each idea reported as one story in the workflow's first state with an issue in each repository it names, once per task name and report number; an idea it refuses is logged and not read again, and a report of another kind is left to the window. A discussion Porelo never records is no longer followed after seven days. Saves and announces nothing itself, and no task events are taken for its offer. The JSON body is at most 65536 bytes; the idea is 1 to 4000 characters and not blank, else InvalidSettings. NoDiscussion (reason) when no sound work rule offers an agent or the brief would exceed 65536 UTF-8 bytes. RecordUnavailable when the offer cannot be recorded.

200.description: The one task to pass to Porelo's Start.

post.summary: Propose the tasks for a story
post.description: Computes a proposal from one board and its sound work rule. The first mode and ordered model entry are the defaults. Only open issues and open sub-issues in their parent's repository participate. Each sub-issue has one helper that builds; reading belongs to the later run. Starts nothing and changes neither state nor revision. The JSON body is at most 65536 bytes. An unknown target state is InvalidSettings.

200.description: The proposed tasks and defaults at this revision.

get.description: Returns null when no run is recorded; working states never recreate a lost record.

200.description: The current work and any still-valid offers.

post.x-mcp: false prepares the tasks only the window starts
post.summary: Prepare the tasks the window starts
post.description: Recomputes the proposal and validates the window's choices against it. Checks the story against the version `seen` holds for it before recorded active work. Omitted repositories and limits take the proposal's defaults; an omitted comment is empty. Every repository and assignment must occur exactly once. Immutable proposal fields must match, KEEP retains the proposed agent and model, CHANGE selects an agent the rule offers for the issues' risk with any model that is a plain name (the rule's model is only the proposal), and DROP leaves the brief to the main task. The main task's agent and model are taken the same way. CHANGE and DROP need a nonblank comment. OTHER may only be dropped. No prompt comes from the body. Expands order placeholders once per task, with repository text delimited by longer backtick fences. Refuses any brief over 4000 characters or task prompt over 65536 UTF-8 bytes. The JSON body is at most 65536 bytes. Persists scoped opaque offers before answering, without starting or moving anything. While the story's run holds offers not started yet, a Start must name that run in `replaces` and then replaces those offers; without `replaces` it is refused with the conflict RunChanged, so a replayed Start never gets a second set of offers to launch. `replaces` naming any other run than the one standing, or a run where none stands, is refused the same way. A `passOver` answers one issue's reason with a new run in place of the old one: it names the run, the issue and its reason (NEXT_STEP_UNAVAILABLE, SAVE_REFUSED, STOPPED or FAILED) as the person saw them, and is refused with RunChanged when the run, or that issue's reason, changed meanwhile, or when another issue of the run needs attention for another reason. BLOCKED is never passed over, since a blocked task said it cannot go on unless something changes. A `passOver` of any reason is refused with WorkNotAllowed while the last ended task of an issue the run raised reports commits unpushed, which only that task can push, and one of FAILED while the failure stopped a reading, which only a reading choice answers. A halted run takes a Start only with a `passOver` of its SAVE_REFUSED, recorded stopped and replaced in one step. A Start without `passOver` over a run any of whose issues holds a reason, a stopped run's STOPPED included, is refused with RunChanged whatever `replaces` names. The run named in `replaces` or `passOver` is checked against the one standing before anything else about it. Work at work, readings waiting for a choice, and lost working records refuse work; every added field is optional.

200.description: The tasks to pass individually to Porelo's Start, at the unchanged revision.

get.description: Answers one issue with its text, its sub-issues and its What must be true paragraph when it has one. An id two issues share answers NoSuchIssue, since no one issue is meant.

200.description: The issue at the given revision.

put.description: Writes the issue's worker into its head, checked against the version `seen` holds for the issue, saved as a move is saved: one commit in the planner's own clone, pushed after the answer under the person's own Git login, or nothing at all. A worker equal to the issue's is saved as nothing. A sub-issue takes its parent's worker and is refused one of its own; an issue a task of a running work owns, itself or through one of its sub-issues, is refused, as a move of it is. An issue a person works is refused an agent while it or one of its sub-issues stands in a working state, which no task entered.

200.description: The worker is saved, or was the issue's already.

put.summary: Set an issue's size, estimate, priority and rank
put.description: Writes the members the body names, checked against the version `seen` holds for the issue: a member left out stays as it is, and null clears a size, an estimate or a rank; a priority is never cleared, and a body naming no field is refused. Values equal to the issue's save nothing and answer the current revision. The JSON body is at most 65536 bytes. The changes stream announces the new board as it does after any save.

200.description: The fields are saved, or held those values already.

put.summary: Set the issues an issue waits on
put.description: Writes the issue's whole list of blockers, checked against the version `seen` holds for the issue; whether the list leads back to the issue is judged on the blockers as they stand at the write: a blocker taken out no longer blocks it, one added does. Each blocker is named once, is one of the board's issues and is not the issue itself; a list that would make an issue wait on itself through its blockers, or that adds or takes out a blocker a warning holds back, is refused (EditNotAllowed) before anything is written. A list equal to the issue's saves nothing and answers the current revision. The JSON body is at most 65536 bytes. The changes stream announces the new board as it does after any save.

200.description: The blockers are saved, or were the issue's already.

put.summary: Set an issue's title and text
put.description: Writes the issue's title and the named parts of its text the body names, every other byte of the text as it was: what it covers, Why this size, What must be true, Plan, Acceptance, Open questions, To be checked and Findings. A member left out stays as it is; null removes the part with its lead or heading, except what the issue covers and What must be true, whose null is refused, and the title, which is never removed. Also needs, a person's own headings, the fields and the stage comments are not written by this call; a member naming them is refused (EditNotAllowed), and a body naming nothing is refused. The member labels sets the item's topic labels (TopicLabels): a label outside them that the item carries stays, and a name outside them is refused (LabelNotAllowed) before anything is written. The Git store sets no labels (NotOffered). On GitHub the item is read back after the write, since GitHub drops labels without an error for an account that may not set them; labels it carries other than every label sent - the topic labels asked and those of the person's own it carried - are refused (LabelsNotKept, naming the repository and the item), never answered as saved, while what else the edit wrote stands and the changes stream announces it. GitHub matches a label's name in any case, so a label it carries as Tests is the topic label tests: it counts as carried, is taken off when left out, and is never sent beside tests. A topic label the repository lacks is created by GitHub for the write in its own grey without a description and stays so: the next Refresh shows it as differing in the repository's warning, whose Labels correction sets it right. A text and labels equal to the item's save nothing and answer the current revision. The edit is checked against the version `seen` holds for the item, and on GitHub the item is read again right before the write and the edit refused (ItemChanged, naming the item) when a person changed it since; GitHub takes no condition on an issue's update, so a change made in the one round trip between that read and the write is overwritten, and stays in GitHub's own history of the item. A part whose text holds a line Markdown reads as a heading of the first or second level, a lead of another leading part, a blank line in a leading part, a code block, an HTML comment, a pre or a details block left open, or a text that would grow the body past the 65536 characters GitHub takes, is refused (EditNotAllowed) before anything is written; so is a body whose sections cannot be told apart for certain, with the first thing to repair. The JSON body is at most 267264 bytes. The changes stream announces the new board as it does after any save.

200.description: The text is saved, or held it already.

post.summary: Write a comment on an issue
post.description: Writes one comment of the person's text on the issue, with the person's own access. The board shows no comment, so the call carries no versions, the board is not read again and the changes stream announces nothing. A comment opening with the planner's own marker `<!-- porelo:` is refused, since the planner reads its own records from such comments. The JSON body is at most 267264 bytes. A comment the tracker took without answering is answered PartlySaved, so it is not written twice.

put.description: Writes the story's priority into its head, checked against the version `seen` holds for the story, saved as a move is saved: the head and the stories index in one commit that starts no build, in the planner's own clone, pushed after the answer under the person's own Git login, or nothing at all. A priority equal to the story's is saved as nothing and answers the current revision. The priority touches no issue, so it may change while the story's work runs.

200.description: The priority is saved, or was the story's already.

post.x-mcp: false the save by the digest of a preview the person saw; agents move issues by moveIssues
post.summary: Save moves, all or none
post.description: Checks a batch of moves against the versions `seen` holds for its targets, the preview's `targets`, and the rules against the board as it stands, and saves it all or not at all: each repository it changes gets one commit in the planner's own clone of it. The answer means every commit stands in those clones; the pushes, under the person's own Git login, follow in the background, the other repositories before the project's own, and a push that fails becomes a fault on the board. A story moves its least advanced issues, but a story moved to the completed state (closed, not Rejected) takes no issue along and is refused (MoveNotAllowed) unless each of its issues stands in Review, the state the last work leads to, or closed after the batch; a working state is entered only by work, except by an issue a person works (worker MANUAL), which a person moves into and through the working states by hand, and by an issue an agent works while no run in this planner's record works it or a story holding it, which then reads noRunHere as work started elsewhere; a story enters one only by its work. The body carries the digest of the batch's preview: under the writer lock, before anything is written, the preview is computed again, and a batch whose preview answers another digest is refused (PreviewChanged), so a confirmation counts only for the batch, the repository and the work the person was shown. A batch over running work - a story it moves or moves an issue of whose run has a task at work, or an issue such a task works - is refused (WorkRunning) unless it is confirmed; a confirmed one stops, after its digest matched and in the same step as its save, each run with tasks at work over what moves, as the story's Stop does, and answers those runs with the tasks the window must end, so nothing is stopped that the preview did not show. A move's `reason` is not part of the digest; on a store that keeps reasons (the workflow's `reasons`) it is written as a comment, after the item is closed, on the story whose shown state the move makes its closed state and on each issue the move closes, and once only, so the same move sent again after a save that failed in its comments writes what is missing.

200.description: The moves are saved.

post.x-mcp: false the move preview the person confirms in the window
post.summary: Answer what a batch of moves would do, writing nothing
post.description: Checks a batch of moves as saving it would, against the board as the planner reads it, and answers what it would write and the warnings a person confirms before it is saved: every issue it moves with its repository, old and new state, every story it moves, its warnings, and its targets - every issue and story the batch changes, those a story's move carries along among them - each with its version. Nothing is stopped, written or pushed. The request carries no revision and no versions. The digest answered covers the project's repository and branch, the batch, every target with its version, each from and to state, the warnings and the runs and offers they name, never the board's revision; the save sends it back, and the targets in its `seen`. A refusal the save would answer for the batch itself, such as a working state, an unknown item or an open story moved to another open state, is answered here too. A planner that does not know this operation answers 404, and the window then moves nothing.

200.description: What the batch would do.

post.summary: Answer what the correction of one warning would write, writing nothing
post.description: Checks the correction a warning's `correction` offers, other than a Move, against the board as the planner reads it, with what the person picked among its `choices`, and answers what it would write, its targets with their versions and the digest the save sends back; the request carries no revision and no versions. A Priority of a story and the Labels of a repository are the kinds carried out here; any other is answered NotOffered, and so is a Labels by a store that holds no repository's labels. Nothing is written or pushed. The digest covers the project's repository and branch, the item or the repository corrected, every target with its version, the warning's kind, what the item holds now (`from`), the choice and every call, never the board's revision. While the work rules have faults no correction of an item is offered and one asked for is refused (CorrectionRefused); a repository's correction touches no item and is judged without them. A repository's labels are read anew from its forge, to their last page as every read of them, before its calls are computed, so no call names a label someone deleted or created since they were last read; a read the forge refuses, or of more labels than the planner reads, is refused as a call that cannot be saved (MoveNotAllowed), named by the forge's status alone, and a read the forge does not answer, or refuses for the login, as the store's refusals answer it. A Move is previewed and saved through /moves/preview and /moves, as any move of the issue. The correction is confirmed by the person in the window or by an agent through its tool, which then sends the preview's targets back as `seen` with its digest; a Move warning's correction stays with moveIssues for an agent, and its preview here answers NotOffered.

200.description: What the correction would write.

post.summary: Save the correction of one warning whose preview was confirmed
post.description: Saves the correction its preview showed, once the person in the window or an agent through its tool confirmed it, as a move is saved: one commit in the planner's own clone, pushed after the answer under the person's own Git login, or nothing at all. Under the writer lock, before anything is written, the correction is checked again on the board as it stands: each of the preview's targets must stand at the version `seen` holds for it (ItemChanged; BasisIncomplete for one `seen` lacks), the warning must still stand on the item, no other warning may hold the item back and the work rules may have no faults (CorrectionRefused), and the preview, computed again, must answer the digest sent (PreviewChanged). A stale, changed or repeated confirm so writes nothing. Only the warning corrected is lifted, only for this write; any other warning holds the item as before. A correction never writes a state: a Priority writes the story's priority alone, touches no issue and so neither waits on nor stops a run. A Labels makes exactly the calls its preview listed on the repository's forge, with the person's own login there and in the preview's order, and no commit; it has no targets, so `seen` is exactly `{}`, since a repository has no item version, and any other is refused (MoveNotAllowed, "A repository's correction sends its versions seen as {}."). The repository's labels are read anew from its forge, as for the preview; its warning must still stand, so a second run, once the warning is gone, writes nothing (CorrectionRefused), and the calls computed again from them must answer the digest sent, so labels changed since the preview write nothing (PreviewChanged). A call the forge refuses stops the calls after it and is refused as a call that cannot be saved (MoveNotAllowed), named by the forge's status alone, never its words; the calls made before it stay made, and the repository's labels are read again at the next Refresh.

200.description: The correction is saved.

get.summary: List the issues in no story
get.description: Answers the board's issues that no story names and that are not sub-issues, at any depth, of an issue a story names. An issue in a state the workflow does not have is listed too, with its warning, after those in the workflow's states. Issues follow the board's order of states, then the order in which the store supplies the board's issues. The story query parameter is required and accepts only none; a missing or other value is refused before any board or work record is read (InvalidName). State and repository filter each issue's own fields; values within a filter are alternatives and different filters must all match. Follow next until null with the same filters. The revision identifies store content; live work status may change between pages. Pages contain at most 60,000 JSON characters including their envelope, except an indivisible larger issue, which is answered alone.

parameters.name: story
parameters.description: Selects only issues in no story.

200.description: The issues in no story at the board's revision.

post.summary: Add an idea as a new issue
post.description: Writes a new issue into the named repository of the project, saved as a move is saved; the story it is hung into, when one is named, is its one target, checked against the version `seen` holds for it, and `seen` is otherwise not checked. The Git store writes its file in the first state with the next free number of the repository's first issue prefix, rewrites the repository's issue index and commits in the planner's own clone, pushed after the answer under the person's own Git login. A number an index row still holds is never given again. On every store, a state the workflow lacks is refused with StateNotAllowed (422) before anything is created, and is never repeated. For a GitHub store, the requested state and fields are written in the create's single save, with one revision, and the state is checked as a move is before anything is created: a closed state is refused with StateNotAllowed (422), a working state while a run in this planner's record works the issue's story with EnteredOnlyByWork (422), and other move checks answer 422 with the move's refusal, never PartlySaved; the item parameter is empty because no issue exists yet. A store without creation in a state keeps the create followed by a move, whose failure is PartlySaved. The JSON body is at most 1048576 bytes. A composed GitHub issue body over 65536 characters is refused by the store, never cut. The new issue's topic labels, when named, are set as an edit sets them: the Git store sets none (NotOffered, before anything is created), and on GitHub a label the issue read back does not carry is refused (LabelsNotKept, naming the repository and the new issue, which stands without it). The changes stream announces the new board as it does after any save.

201.description: The issue and its placement are saved; the answer names the resulting board revision.

post.summary: Add an issue made outside the project
post.description: Adds one open issue the board offers among its unlisted issues to the project, checked against the unlisted issue's own version `seen` holds for it, in one save: an issue enters the workflow's first state with Worker Manual, Priority Medium and the rank after the last issue of that priority; a story, an issue of the tracker's issue type Story in the project's own repository, gets Priority Medium and its rank and no state, so its state follows its issues. A store that adds no issue made outside the project answers NotOffered for any issue, before the issue is looked for; the Git store and the mock mode answer so. An issue the board does not offer, one on the board or outside its workflow among them, or one the tracker no longer holds, answers NotUnlisted, and the window reads the board again. On GitHub the issue is read again right before the write: one a person added to the project, closed or moved since the board was read is refused (ItemChanged, naming the issue), and one the board would show only as a warned issue no work starts on once added - a story outside the project's own repository, an issue under an issue that is no item of the project, that the board does not place, that is a sub-issue itself or that is of another repository, an issue blocked by a story or by an item the board does not place, a story that blocks an item of the project - is refused (EditNotAllowed, field issue, naming the warning and what to repair), each before anything is written. A refusal never repeats the tracker's title or text. A failure after GitHub added the issue is PartlySaved, and the issue then stands outside the workflow until its state is moved. The JSON body is at most 65536 bytes. The changes stream announces the new board as it does after any save.

200.description: The issue is saved on the project.

put.x-mcp: false where a local project's items lie is the person's choice on this computer
put.summary: Choose where a local project's stories and issues are kept
put.description: Keeps the directory the planner reads and writes a local project's stories and issues in, for this project, in the planner's own state on this computer and never in the project's files, and reopens the project's store on it; `null` goes back to the default directory. The call is checked in this order: the project's name (InvalidName), the project is known (NoSuchProject), its tracker is `local` (else NotOffered), then the body and the directory (ItemsDirectoryRefused, 400). The body is one JSON object of at most 8192 bytes with exactly the members `directory`, a string or an explicit `null`, and `seen`, an object, and no member twice; it has no target, so its `seen` is not checked against any version. The directory must be an ItemsDirectory that exists, is a directory, is reached through no symbolic link, neither itself nor any directory above it, and is the account's alone, and it is checked again at every read and write; it is never made. A directory refused is answered naming it when it is an ItemsDirectory, and nothing is kept. Choosing the directory in use again keeps nothing anew, reopens nothing and answers the tracker as it stands. Otherwise the project's store is opened anew on the directory, which ends the project's changes streams; a window opens its stream again and is answered the board read from the directory now kept. A write the old store took before the swap ends first; one based on the old store's board that reaches the store after it is refused as Busy, as a save that lost to another, and the window reads the board again. A choice that cannot be written to the planner's state directory is refused as WorkRecordUnavailable, and the project stays as it was. When the directory kept is taken but the project's reads stay refused, as for a default directory outside the rule an ItemsDirectory follows, the choice is kept and the call answers ItemsDirectoryRefused with 409.

200.description: The directory is kept, and the project's tracker as it stands now.

post.x-mcp: false a held save is the person's to send again
post.summary: Send a held save again
post.description: Sends a group of the board's `heldSaves` that is `resendable` again. A window's save turns back to queued and runs again, judged on the versions it was judged on when first sent, never on the board as it stands now; its commands already written are not written again. A run's group, whose task end was refused before it wrote and whose run is not halted, is saved again by its run: the run lands the event it kept against the board as it stands now, once only however often it is sent, as a repeated report is. Either is answered as a move: the revision once the group is written, and the group then leaves `heldSaves`; refused again, it stays there with the new reason, and the refusal is answered. Takes no body. A group that is not refused or held, because it runs or another window resent it, is refused as SaveNotHeld; a halted run's group as SaveOfRun, since the run's own Stop or Start decides it; a group kept from another repository or branch as SaveFromElsewhere, naming that source, since it was never judged against this one. Of a line of folded saves, named by any of its `saves`, the newest group is sent, once; once it is written, the others of the line are dropped, since they would write the same.

200.description: Every command of the group is written.

delete.x-mcp: false a held save is the person's to drop
delete.description: Removes a group of the board's `heldSaves` from the outbox, a halted run's and one kept from another source among them, writing nothing to the store; what its commands wrote before they were held stays written. The planner's log names the group's id and its commands' targets. No other call removes a held group. A group that is not refused or held, because it runs or another window resent it, is refused as SaveNotHeld. Of a line of folded saves, every group of the line is dropped.

parameters.name: task
parameters.description: The task's name within the project, as Start took it and Porelo lists it in a task's task field; never its container, which the body's container names.

post.x-mcp: false the window reports the tasks it started
post.summary: Report the lifecycle of an offered task
post.description: Accepts STARTED, ENDED, STOPPED, LANDED or REFUSED against an offer. Only ENDED carries Porelo's unmapped ended record. STARTED binds task and container once. REFUSED reports that Porelo refused the Start of the offered task, sent once per refusal after the window called Start and again at its next sweep until answered; it carries the refusal and no container, since no task started. The offer stays offered, and a later Start of it is still possible, which clears the refusal; the issues of the offer ask the person with START_REFUSED, and the refusal's name, parameters and words stand in `startRefusal` of each. A rework at the place its issue keeps that is refused as NotTheTasksPush says the place changed instead, as PLACE_CHANGED. The planner judges no name: any well-shaped one stands as given. REFUSED for an offer that ended, or that already stands refused, is a resend, answered with what stands and recorded once; for an offer Porelo started it is refused as TaskEventConflict. LANDED reports once where a build's work landed after its ENDED, when that end named no landing; only then is the build's reader offered. LANDED for an unknown offer, an offer that did not end done, or one that already landed is refused as TaskEventConflict, so a resend changes nothing. Unknown, void or foreign offers and contradictory bindings are refused. Identical reports replay their disposition after restart, without saving or counting twice, and return only still-valid offers. The report is at most 131072 bytes, its answer at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes. Every save refusal halts the run and voids unstarted work. A late end after cancellation only clears activity. An ENDED of a task whose rule hands back a result moves none of its issues, whatever its outcome: a saved result moved them already, and without one they stay with NEXT_STEP_UNAVAILABLE and one line why.

200.description: The current work and any still-valid offers.

post.x-mcp: false the window hands in a task's result
post.summary: Hand in the result a stage's task wrote
post.description: Takes the result file an analysis, estimation or readiness task wrote, which the window hands in unchanged with the task's offer while the task is at work, before its ENDED; or, when the task left no readable file, one line why it is missing. Only a started offer of the project's run, bound to this task, whose rule hands back a result is taken; an unknown, void or foreign offer is refused as TaskNotAnswered, and an offer whose task hands back no result (a reader's, or one of work that pushes) or is not at work as ResultRefused, both recording nothing. The result is checked before anything is saved: its format and kind match the rule, it names exactly the offer's issues, each once, every member follows the result format, and no text holds a control or direction character but a newline in a plan. Each issue must still belong to the offer, stand in the state the stage works in and be worked by an agent. A sound result is saved through the store in one save on the store as it stands, each issue moving from that state to the rule's done state, and for a readiness check each issue not ready back to the rule's one from state instead, with why kept beside it; a result refused, or one missing, saves nothing and its issues stay where they stand, under Needs you once the task ended. One offer has one outcome: the first hand-in's - saved, missing, or the refusal with its faults - is recorded, and a second hand-in of the same offer answers it again and writes nothing, whatever it holds; a save that failed or did not end is recorded as a refusal, but for a store that refuses before it writes anything: busy or moved, which records nothing, so the same result is handed in again later; or without the person's access to the forge (NoForgeAccess), which keeps the result waiting, so the same result is handed in again once a token is handed on, even after the task's ENDED. A stage task's ENDED never moves its issues; an ENDED of an offer with no hand-in records its result as missing. The JSON body is at most 1052672 bytes. The changes stream announces the new board after a save.

200.description: The offer's outcome, by this hand-in or an earlier one of the same offer.

post.x-mcp: false the person cancels a run in the window, which stops its tasks
post.summary: Cancel the run
post.description: Takes an empty body, or one naming the run the person saw in `run`; a run named that is not the one standing, or a run named where none stands, is refused with the conflict RunChanged. Records cancellation of a run at work, ended with reasons or halted, and voids unstarted offers, retaining states, counts and findings; every reason then reads STOPPED. Active tasks stay at work until the window stops them and reports STOPPED or a late ENDED. Repeatable.

200.description: The current work and any still-valid offers.

post.x-mcp: false the person chooses how a stopped reading goes on
post.summary: Choose how a stopped reading continues
post.description: Checks story membership, stopped status, exact completed round and the versions `seen` holds for its targets: the issue and every deferred issue of the story it reconciles, so a window sends the versions of the story's issues. The choice clears the stop before an offer leaves. REVIEW_ANYWAY retains findings and saves the rule's done state. ONE_MORE_ROUND offers a reader in the Reading rule's first mode and model, granting one more reading only at the limit; REWORK offers rework with the saved blocking findings and the operator's words, which it requires only when no saved finding blocks, in the given mode, agent and model or else the Reworking rule's first ones. A reading stopped as INVALID_FINDINGS, whose findings could not be read, or by a reader that ended FAILED or BLOCKED, takes ONE_MORE_ROUND, a new reader of the same build, and REVIEW_ANYWAY; it refuses REWORK as ReworkNeedsFindings, since nothing guides it. It keeps no findings, as no other stopped reading does, so it is known by that once a failed choice has renamed its reason NEXT_STEP_UNAVAILABLE. Neither counts a reading. Stopped or halted runs refuse choices. The body is at most 65536 bytes.

200.description: The current work and any still-valid offers.

get.x-mcp: false the description itself, which a caller reads to make its tools
get.description: Answers this description as JSON, converted from the YAML the planner was built with when it was built, member for member: every operation with its `x-mcp` marker, `true` for an operation an agent may call as a tool, or a string opening with `false` and the reason it is not offered to agents. A build whose description holds an operation without one marker fails.

200.description: The description the planner was built with.

get.description: Answers the board the planner holds in short, without reading the store anew: each story with its id, title, state and priority and each of its issues with its id, state, size and priority, in the board's order, then the issues no story names that are not sub-issues of an issue a story names. What it says of an item equals what the board says of it at the same revision. State and priority select each story's own fields and each loose issue's own fields; repository selects a story when any of its issues is of that repository, and a loose issue by its own repository. All of a selected story's issues are included. Values within a filter are alternatives; different filters must all match. Follow next until null with the same filters. A story is never split. Pages contain at most 60,000 JSON characters including their envelope, except an indivisible larger item, which is answered alone.

200.description: The board in short at the given revision.

get.summary: Read one issue by its text's parts
get.description: Answers one issue of the board the planner holds with its fields and its text split into the parts setIssueText writes, each by the same name; a part the text does not hold is absent. A text whose sections cannot be told apart for certain answers its parts as null and the whole text in `text`, with the first thing to repair in `fault`. An id two issues share answers NoSuchIssue.

200.description: The issue at the given revision.

get.summary: The breaches of the stories' rules
get.description: Answers the breaches of the stories' rules as the board the planner holds computes them, the board's `rules` grouped: each with its rule, the story it concerns (null for an issue in no story) and the issues it names, in the board's order. An empty list means the board breaks none.

200.description: The breaches at the given revision.

get.summary: Find stories and issues by words
get.description: Answers the stories and issues of the board the planner holds whose title or text holds every word given, matched without regard to case as a whole word, each with its id, kind, title, state and where the words were found: `title`, or the name of the text part as setIssueText names it, or `text` for a story's text and a text whose parts cannot be told apart. Stories come first, then issues, each in the board's order; at most 200 are answered per page and more says whether next is non-null. Follow next until null with the same words to reach every match. Pages contain at most 60,000 JSON characters including their envelope, except an indivisible larger match, which is answered alone. Nothing is read from the store anew.

200.description: The matching items at the given revision.

post.summary: Move many issues to their states, saving what the rules allow
post.description: Moves many issues to their states in one call, by the rules saveMoves keeps: the planner previews the batch on the board as it stands, drops each move the rules refuse with its refusal, and saves the rest in one save against the board it previewed, all or none; a move into a state only a person sets is refused as the rules say, and a move that would stop running work is refused (WorkRunning), since no person confirms it here. A board changed between the preview and the save is previewed again once; changed again, nothing is saved and the call answers ItemChanged. The answer names every issue sent once, in the order sent: SAVED with its new state, UNCHANGED when it stood there already, or REFUSED with the refusal as the call alone would have answered it. A batch the rules refuse whole saves nothing and answers 200 with every issue REFUSED. The JSON body is at most 65536 bytes. The changes stream announces the new board as it does after any save.

200.description: What was saved and what refused, per issue.

post.summary: Apply new and changed issues in one call
post.description: Applies a board change in one call: new issues, each named by a key of the caller's, and changes of existing issues. Every item is judged by the rules the window's own calls keep (createIssue, setIssueText, setIssueFields, setWorker, setBlockedBy, setStoryIssues and moveIssues) against the board as it stands, before anything is written; then the new issues are made, then the blockers, story lists, fields and states are written, in one save where the store allows it. A blocker or story is named by an existing id or by a key of the same body, resolved to the id made for it. A key is never an id of the board and an issue is changed once in a body, else the whole body is refused (EditNotAllowed). Before anything is written every item is judged on what needs no write, by the rules of the calls named: each text part, each blocker (not the issue itself, an issue of the board or a new issue, none twice, none leading back through the board's blockers and the body's own), a story that is a story of the board, and a state of the workflow; the refusal is the one the call alone would give. An item refused never stops the others; an item whose blocker or story is a key of a refused item, one listed after it included, is refused naming that key (KeyRefused, item and key), and a key naming no item of the body is refused naming it (NoSuchKey, item and key). A refusal or failure of the store for one item never ends the call: the item is REFUSED with it, and once the store cannot be reached or is busy the items after it are refused with the same, untried. An item whose later step is refused after an earlier step of it was written is REFUSED as PartlySaved, `issues` naming it and the detail the steps that stand and the refusal of the next. The answer names every item once, new issues first in the order sent, each with its key, its id when it stands and SAVED, UNCHANGED or REFUSED with the refusal; SAVED is told by whether a step of the item wrote. The JSON body is at most 1048576 bytes. The changes stream announces the new board as it does after any save.

200.description: What was saved and what refused, per item.

put.summary: Set priority, size and story of many issues, and stories' priorities, in one save
put.description: Sets the priority, size or story of many issues and the priority of stories in one save, against the board as it stands, by the rules setIssueFields, setStoryIssues and setPriority keep; a member left out stays as it is. A story's priority set also raises, in the same save, each of its issues whose priority would then break the stories' priority rule, and names them in its result's `raised`; an issue sent in the same body keeps the priority sent for it, and a breach that leaves is refused for that issue. An issue given a story leaves its old story and joins the new one, as setStoryIssues moves it. The answer names every item once, issues first, in the order sent: SAVED, UNCHANGED or REFUSED with the refusal; an item refused never stops the others. The JSON body is at most 65536 bytes. The changes stream announces the new board as it does after any save.

200.description: What was saved and what refused, per item.

signature.name: Porelo-Signature
signature.description: The HMAC-SHA256 of the request under the token the planner was started with, as the description of the API gives its form; the token itself is never sent. A missing, malformed, repeated, late or replayed signature, or one over anything but the request as sent, answers 401.

PageLimit.name: limit
PageLimit.description: Maximum top-level items on this page; the character bound may end it earlier.

PageAfter.name: after
PageAfter.description: Opaque next cursor from the preceding page of this project and read, with the same filters or search words. Invalid cursors or changed selections answer InvalidName (400); a changed store revision answers PageChanged (409), requiring a restart without after. The cursor is a continuation, not an authorization credential.

ReadState.name: state
ReadState.description: Select these states; repeated values are alternatives, absent selects all.

ReadPriority.name: priority
ReadPriority.description: Select these priorities; repeated values are alternatives, absent selects all.

ReadRepository.name: repository
ReadRepository.description: Select these repository names; repeated values are alternatives, absent selects all.

Story.name: story
Story.description: The story's identifier. The `#` of a tracker reference is percent-encoded in the path, `%23`, as is any other character a path segment cannot carry; the planner decodes the segment before it checks the id.

Issue.name: issue
Issue.description: The issue's identifier. The `#` of a tracker reference is percent-encoded in the path, `%23`, as is any other character a path segment cannot carry; the planner decodes the segment before it checks the id.

Save.name: save
Save.description: The id of a held save, as the board's `heldSaves` names it.

RunConflict.description: ItemChanged(changed[],items[]), BasisIncomplete(missing[]), WorkRunning(story,tasks[]), ReadingNotStopped(issue), ReadingRoundChanged(issue,rounds), ReworkNeedsFindings(issue), TaskEventConflict(task,event,reason) or RunChanged(story,reason). Subjects are checked before echoing. On a local project, also ItemsDirectoryRefused(directory) while the directory kept for its stories and issues, or its default directory, can no longer be used, as that response says.

RecordUnavailable.description: Busy(repository) or WorkRecordUnavailable(project,reason). The record reason says why in words: fixed words and, where a directory or file was refused, that path named relative to the home directory (~/...) or to the state directory ($XDG_STATE_HOME/... or %LOCALAPPDATA%\...), never as an absolute path, and never the record's content.

WorkRefused.description: InvalidName for an invalid path id (only a checked project may be echoed); InvalidSettings for malformed JSON, an oversized body, path/body disagreement or an unknown target state, with a fixed detail; WorkNotAllowed for a missing or unsound rule, disallowed from or mode, altered proposal facts, invalid choices or limits, or bounds; NoDiscussion for a discussion no sound rule offers an agent for, or whose brief is too long, with reason. WorkNotAllowed parameters are from, to and reason; to is always a known workflow state. A changed helper identity or brief has reason 'A helper identity or brief was changed.'. InvalidSettings parameters contain detail.

WorkConflict.description: ItemChanged names the story when it changed since the version `seen` holds for it, with the story as it stands; BasisIncomplete names it when `seen` holds no version for it. WorkRunning names the checked story and an array of recorded active task names. RunChanged(story,reason) says in fixed words that the run a Start names in `replaces` or `passOver`, or the reason it passes over, is not the one standing, or that the run holds a reason a Start must pass over. The story's version is checked first; a story's state alone never means work is running. On a local project, also ItemsDirectoryRefused(directory) while the directory kept for its stories and issues, or its default directory, can no longer be used, as that response says.

Unauthorized.description: The request carries no one valid signature, carries an Authorization header, or has a body larger than 267264 bytes (1048576 bytes for POST on new stories and new issues, 1052672 bytes for a stage's result); the body is empty, and the answer carries no Porelo-Answer header.

WWW-Authenticate.description: Names the form of signature the planner expects.

InvalidLevel.description: The level is none of ERROR, WARN, INFO and DEBUG (InvalidLevel); the level in force stays.

example.title: InvalidLevel
example.detail: The level is none of ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG.

PageTooLarge.description: Mandatory page metadata alone exceeds 60,000 JSON characters (PageTooLarge); for full story lists, use getOutline, which omits the whole-board open counts. No incomplete or oversized metadata is returned.

example.title: PageTooLarge
example.detail: The page metadata exceeds the answer bound; read the board outline instead.

PageConflict.description: PageChanged when the store revision differs from the cursor's revision; discard all pages and read again from the start. ItemsDirectoryRefused retains the directory refusal described by ItemsDirectoryRefused when the local store cannot be read.

value.title: PageChanged
value.detail: The board changed since the first page; read again from its start.

InvalidName.description: A project name, story id, issue id or query parameter was refused (InvalidName); its parameters name the project, unless the project's own name is the one refused.

example.title: InvalidName
example.detail: The story id is not a valid id.

ProjectRefused.description: The project, its branch or its repository was refused: InvalidName for a project or branch name, NotACloneUrl for a repository that is not a clone URL.

value.title: InvalidName
value.detail: The branch name is not a valid name.

value.title: NotACloneUrl
value.detail: The repository is not a clone URL.

NoSuchProject.description: The project was never made known with a PUT (NoSuchProject).

NoSuchStory.description: The project is not known (NoSuchProject) or has no such story (NoSuchStory).

value.title: NoSuchProject
value.detail: The project is not known.

value.title: NoSuchStory
value.detail: The project has no such story.

NoSuchIssue.description: The project is not known (NoSuchProject) or has no such issue (NoSuchIssue).

value.title: NoSuchProject
value.detail: The project is not known.
