Name.description: The name of a project or a repository.

StoryId.description: A story's identifier in one of two forms: the Git store's, ST and a number, or a tracker reference within the project, `<repository>#<number>`, the repository's name as Name takes it, without `..`, and the tracker's number of one to nine digits without a leading zero. A store answers only its own form.

TextFormat.description: The format a store writes its texts in, an open name: MARKDOWN for the Git store, PLAIN, or a store's own. A reader shows a format it does not know as plain text.

IssueId.description: An issue's identifier in one of two forms: the Git store's, a prefix and a number, with a sub-issue's number after a dot, or a tracker reference within the project, `<repository>#<number>`, the repository's name as Name takes it, without `..`, and the tracker's number of one to nine digits without a leading zero. A store answers only its own form.

RunId.description: A story's run, drawn by the planner when the run starts and kept while it stands; opaque to the window, which compares it only for equality.

SaveId.description: A save's group of commands, drawn by the planner when the window's save is taken; opaque to the window, which compares it only for equality and sends it back to resend or drop the group.

Revision.description: The store's revision the answer was read at; opaque to the window, which compares it only for equality. At most 200 printable characters without spaces, however many repositories the project has, since the window sends it back as the `Last-Event-ID` header; the Git store gives a SHA-256 as 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters.

Version.description: An item's own stored edit basis, opaque to the window, which compares it only for equality: two equal versions of one item mean its own stored state is unchanged. A value it takes from another item, such as a sub-issue's inherited worker or a story's state its issues give, is not part of it; neither is a comment or another item's change. 40 or 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters: the Git store gives the id of an item's file in Git where it has one, and otherwise, as every other store, a SHA-256 of the item's own stored state.

WrittenVersions.description: The new version of each item a write changed, by item id, read from the board the save left, in the form `seen` takes: the items the write targets, any item it made, and every story that held or now holds an issue it wrote, so a next write that changes such a story's list finds its version here. A caller sends its next write's `seen` from it and needs no read between two writes. An item the board no longer holds as one item is left out. If the read-back fails, items whose new versions are unknown are left out. A write that changes nothing answers its targets' current versions. The keys are the planner's own item ids, so no pattern is repeated for them here and an agent's tool takes the answer whole.

Seen.description: The versions the person saw, by item id: the edit basis a write is checked against. The planner determines the write's targets, the items whose own stored state it changes, each request schema naming them; a target whose version here differs from the one it stands at is refused (ItemChanged), and a target without an entry is refused (BasisIncomplete), never taken as one not to check. An entry for an item that is no target is not checked, so a window may send the version of every item it showed. Always present; `{}` for a write without targets. At most 2000 entries, so the check of one write never holds an unbounded map: the most targets a write can name, a full batch of moves each carrying its story's issues, is far larger, while a window sends the versions of the items it acts on; an object of more entries is refused like one that names no versions.

LabelName.description: A label's name as the tracker holds it: 1 to 50 characters, GitHub's own limit, without a control character, a character that hides or turns text - a format, zero-width or bidi character, a soft hyphen (U+00AD), a combining grapheme joiner (U+034F), the Mongolian vowel separator (U+180E) or a tag character (U+E0000 to U+E007F) -, or a line or paragraph separator. The pattern is read without the u flag, so a tag character stands in it as its UTF-16 surrogate pair.

Labels.description: An item's labels on its tracker, in the store's order, each at most once: the topic labels and any label of the person's own, which the planner shows and keeps but never sets. A label the tracker holds whose name is no LabelName is left out here and stays on the tracker, never written. Empty where the store holds none, as the Git store.

TopicLabel.description: One of the seven topic labels every repository of a project carries, the labels the planner sets.

TopicLabels.description: The topic labels an item carries after the write, each at most once: a topic label named is put on, one left out is taken off, and a label outside the topic labels that the item carries already stays as it is. A name outside the topic labels is refused, as LabelNotAllowed on an edit and as IssueNotAllowed (field labels) on a new issue, and so is a name given twice (EditNotAllowed or IssueNotAllowed, field labels).

Target.description: An item a write changes, with the version it stands at.

id.description: An issue's or a story's id.

ChangedItem.description: A target an ItemChanged refusal names, as the store holds it now: exactly one of issue, story and unlisted, with gone false; or gone true and none of them when the store holds no one readable item by that id any more.

level.description: How much the planner's log holds, the least first; INFO when none was set.

version.description: The planner's package version, as its .deb and .rpm carry it.

commit.description: The commit the planner was built from; null for a build without a Git checkout.

ProofRequest.description: A caller's challenge, 32 random bytes in canonical base64url without padding.

Proof.description: The planner's proof that it holds the token, for the port it listens on and the challenge.

ProjectSource.description: Where a project's planning is kept.

repository.description: The project's own repository's clone URL, as https://host/path, ssh://[user@]host/path or user@host:path.

branch.description: The branch to read and write; the repository's default branch when absent.

faults.description: What was found wrong reading the workflow, and each story, issue or reference left out because it could not be read, in the planner's words. The rest of the board is answered.

reasons.description: Whether the store keeps a move's `reason` with the item it closes; a window offers the reason only when true and reads an answer without it as false.

kind.description: CLOSED when the workflow closes the state, WORKING when a sound work rule exists for it, else WAITING.

measured.description: Whether moving an issue into the state needs a stage record. An open story's state is derived from its issues by the measured states alone: building starts in the first measured open state, the open state before it is the backlog, and a story waits for review in the last of the measured open states that run on from there.

Phase.description: One column of the board and its states.

states.description: The names of the column's states, in order.

WorkRule.description: How work is done in a working state.

from.description: The states work may start from.

done.description: The state a story or issue reaches when the work is done.

then.description: The state that follows the done state, or null when none does.

blocked.description: The state a blocked work goes to, or null when none is named.

per.description: Whether one task works the whole story or one each repository.

modes.description: The ways the work may run, such as SHELL, AGENT or UNATTENDED.

order.description: The work order given to the task.

models.description: The model for each agent, in order of preference.

Board.description: The whole board at one revision, as an event of the stream carries it - the workflow, the project's repositories, the stories and the issues in no story.

repositories.description: The project's repositories, its own first, the others in the order project.yml names them; a new issue may be added in each of them, whether or not a story names an issue of it.

repositoryWarnings.description: What the store found wrong in the project's repositories themselves, at most one warning of a kind per repository, in the order of `repositories`; empty when nothing. The GitHub store compares each repository's labels with the topic labels at the project's first read and at each Refresh, and one repository's again at the preview and the confirm of its correction, and keeps what it found between them, so a plain read of the board reads no repository's labels; a store that holds no repository's labels, the Git and the local store, answers it empty.

faults.description: What was found wrong reading the workflow, and each story, issue or reference left out because it could not be read, in the planner's words. The rest of the board is answered.

reasons.description: Whether the store keeps a move's `reason` with the item it closes; a window offers the reason only when true and reads an answer without it as false.

unlisted.description: The open issues of the project's repositories that are no items of the project, as one made by hand on the tracker is, in the order of the repositories. None of them is on the board. Empty when there are none; a store without a tracker answers it empty, and a window reads an answer without it as empty.

open.description: What is still open of the whole board, as the story list answers it.

rules.description: Every breach of the stories' rules on this board, the stories' in the board's order and then the issues', the same rules whichever store keeps the project. Unlike `faults`, a breach leaves nothing out, and it is only shown: no move, preview or save reads it, and none is refused or warned for it. The whole board carries it, and a delta replaces the list when it changes; a window that reads none shows none.

heldSaves.description: Every save the project's outbox keeps refused or held for the person, the groups written to this project's repository and branch first, in the order they were taken, then those kept from another source; empty when nothing is held, and on a store whose saves go through no outbox. A group stays here until it is resent and written whole, or dropped.

noStory.description: The issues in no story, directly or through a parent, exactly as listIssues with story=none answers them at this revision: by workflow state, then the store's priority and rank, including warned rows with duplicate ids.

BoardDelta.description: The difference from the last Board answer sent on this connection. Apply only when both `after` and `before` match the frame and revision held; otherwise read the whole Board again by reconnecting. The initial Board is frame 0. Each sent change increments frame by one. The new revision can equal before for a work-only change. Stories and noStory replace all rows of each id supplied, in occurrence order; removed ids remove every row of that id. A changed group includes every current row of its id, preserving duplicate ids. Order lists give the whole new order, repeating duplicate ids; consume each id's rows in their supplied occurrence order. Without an order list retain the old order. Other absent members retain their old values; present members replace them whole, including empty lists and false.

stories.description: New or changed stories, each whole with its issues; empty when none changed.

noStory.description: New or changed issues in no story; empty when none changed.

removedIssues.description: Ids no longer in noStory, including issues that joined a story.

RuleBreach.description: One breach of the stories' rules. IssueInNoStory - an issue that is not closed stands in a state past the workflow's first and in no story, directly or under a parent. StoryPriorityBelowIssue - a story's priority is below the highest priority of its open issues, its sub-issues included; an issue without a priority is not ranked.

item.description: The story's or the issue's id.

words.description: The breach in the planner's fixed words, naming items only by their ids.

HeldSave.description: One save the outbox keeps for the person, a group of commands not written whole: refused by the store before it wrote, or held after a command that may stand in part. Every group can be dropped; one that is `resendable` can also be resent. Groups each of whose one command not yet written makes exactly one change, to the same field of the same item and the same value, with the same run, earlier flag, repository and branch, fold into one line, told by its newest group: its id, reason, changes, commands and flags, with the tries of every group folded. A group with more than one command not yet written, or whose one command makes no change or more than one, stays a line of its own.

saves.description: Every group folded into the line, oldest first, its `id` last; the one group alone when nothing folds with it.

reason.description: Why the save is held, in one plain sentence of the planner's fixed words for the reason of its first command refused or held, naming what the reason is about where there is something.

changes.description: What the save would change, for every command of it not yet written, in their order: one line per field of an item. Empty when its commands change no field the board names, as a comment, a new item or a repository's labels do.

answer.description: The forge's answer to the save's last try, as that try keeps it; absent when the last try kept none, as for a refusal the planner made itself, or when the save has no try.

tries.description: Every try of the save that ended refused or held, oldest first, each kept with its time, how it ended, why and the forge's answer; at most the newest 1000, the older left out. Empty for a save kept before its tries were.

run.description: Whether the group is a run's: either a halted run's, which the run's own Stop or Start decides, or one whose task end was refused before it wrote while its run goes on, which its run saves again on a resend.

earlier.description: Whether the group was kept from another repository or branch the project named before; it is never run against this one, so it can be dropped but not resent.

resendable.description: Whether the group can be resent, as the planner judges it: true for a window's save, and for a run's group whose task end was refused before it wrote while the run is not halted; false for a halted run's group and for one kept from another source. A window offers Resend only when true.

repository.description: The clone URL of the repository the group was to be written to; present only when `earlier`.

branch.description: The branch the group was to be written to; present only when `earlier` and that source named a branch.

commands.description: Every command of the group in its order, those already written included.

HeldChange.description: One field of one item a held save would change: the value it would write, and the value GitHub held at the planner's last read of the board. `now` and `nowAt` are both absent when the item was never read or the store tells no time of its read, and for a value the board does not hold, such as an item's text; `nowUnset` and `nowAt` tell a value read and empty.

target.description: The issue or story the field belongs to, by its id.

field.description: The field by the name its item carries it under on the board (state, worker, priority, size, title, labels, blockedBy, issues), or for a value the board does not hold by its own name (reason, estimateMinutes, rank, and a text part such as whatMustBeTrue).

now.description: The value at the planner's last read; a list joined by a comma and a blank. Absent when not known or read empty.

nowUnset.description: True when the value was read and empty; absent otherwise.

nowAt.description: When the board holding `now` was read, in UTC; present exactly when `now` or `nowUnset` is.

saved.description: The value the save would write; a list joined by a comma and a blank. Absent when the save removes or empties the value.

HeldTry.description: One try of a held save that ended refused or held.

at.description: When the try ended, in UTC.

result.description: REFUSED when the store refused it before it wrote anything; HELD when it may stand in part.

reason.description: Why the try ended so, in one plain sentence of the planner's fixed words, as a save's `reason` is.

answer.description: The forge's answer to the try; absent when it gave none.

HeldAnswer.description: The forge's own answer to a call that was refused, word for word: its message and further words joined by a semicolon and a blank, with any token removed and control characters escaped, at most 4096 bytes in UTF-8.

status.description: The HTTP status the forge answered with; 0 when it answered none.

text.description: The forge's words; empty when it gave none.

requestId.description: The id the forge gave the request, for its support; absent when it gave none.

HeldCommand.description: One command of a held save, told by its kind, its target and where it stands; what it would change is in its save's `changes`.

id.description: The command's id, its group's id and its place in the group.

kind.description: What the command writes: WRITE a move's states, workers, priorities and reasons; SET_FIELDS an issue's fields; SET_TEXT an item's title and text; SET_BLOCKERS an issue's blockers; SET_STORY_ISSUES a story's issues; CORRECT_LABELS a repository's labels; COMMENT a comment; CREATE_ISSUE, CREATE_IDEA and CREATE_STORY a new item; ADD_UNLISTED an issue made outside the project.

target.description: The issue or story the command writes, or for CORRECT_LABELS and a new item the repository it writes to, by its name as Name takes it, without `..`.

state.description: QUEUED waits for the commands before it; DONE is written; REFUSED was refused by the store before it wrote anything; HELD may stand in part, or waits behind a command that does.

reason.description: Why the command is refused or held, as the store's refusal of that name; NotOffered for a failure that is none of them, NONE for a command queued or done.

subject.description: What the reason is about, cleaned as every refusal's words are: at most 256 characters, no control, format, private-use, unassigned or separator character and no blank that shows as nothing; empty when the reason names nothing or its words were not clean.

UnlistedIssue.description: An open issue of one of the project's repositories that is no item of the project. Its title is the tracker's text, shown as plain text.

kind.description: An open name of what the issue is; a window shows a kind it does not know as an issue. Known kinds are story, when the tracker's issue type is Story and the issue is in the project's own repository, and issue otherwise.

link.description: The issue on the tracker, built from its repository and number.

author.description: The login of the account that opened the issue, shown as plain text; left out when the tracker named none of a login's form, as for an account the tracker no longer holds; the window then shows no author.

authorAssociation.description: How that account stands to the issue's repository, as the tracker names it, shown as plain text; left out when the tracker named none of these; the window then shows none.

Moves.description: A batch of moves with the versions seen, its preview's targets, and the digest of its preview; a batch that confirms its warnings may leave the digest out, and the planner's preview of the same moves stands for it.

confirm.description: Whether the person confirmed the preview's warnings: each run its RUNNING_WORK warning named is stopped with the save.

MovesPreviewRequest.description: A batch of moves to preview against the board as the planner reads it; it carries no versions.

PreviewDigest.description: A SHA-256 over what a preview showed, as 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters; opaque to the window, which only sends it back with the save.

MovePreview.description: What a batch of moves would write, and what a person confirms before it is saved.

targets.description: Every issue and story the batch changes, each once with the version it stands at: those it moves and the issues a story's move carries along. The save sends them back in `seen`.

issues.description: Every issue the batch moves, each once, in the order the save names them.

warnings.description: What the batch can do harm by; empty when it is saved without asking. A window lists under RUNNING_WORK too the tasks it started that the planner does not know yet; the digest does not cover those.

MovedIssue.description: An issue a batch moves, or one a warning names, with its state now and after the batch.

MovedStory.description: A story a batch moves, with the state it shows now and the one it is moved to.

MoveWarning.description: One harm a batch can do. RUNNING_WORK - a story's run has tasks at work over what moves, the story itself or an issue of it: item is the story, run its run, tasks each task at work and offers each offer not yet started, all of which its stop ends or voids; an unconfirmed save is refused (WorkRunning), a confirmed one stops them. ISSUES_ALONG - a story's move carries issues along that stand in a working state or in another repository than the project's own: item is the story, issues each such issue. SKIPS_STATES - a move forward past waiting states: item is the story or issue, from and to its states, skipped the states passed.

item.description: The story or issue the warning is about.

to.description: The state the batch moves the item to.

run.description: The run whose tasks RUNNING_WORK names, or null.

Move.description: One move, naming exactly one story or one issue. A story is moved only to close it or, once closed, to reopen it: an open story follows its issues, and its move to another open state is refused (MoveNotAllowed). Its move to the workflow's first closed state closes it as completed and closes with it each of its issues in Review; to a later closed state, closes it as not planned and closes with it each of its issues in an open state of the workflow. Its move to an open state reopens it alone.

issue.description: An issue of the board. One warned StateOutsideWorkflow moves from the state it stands in into a state of the workflow, which repairs it, under the same rules as any issue (a working state only for an issue a person works or one no run in this planner's record works).

reason.description: The person's one sentence why the item is closed: what was built, or why not. Taken only on a move into a closed state and optional there, a blank one counting as none; a story's reason is given to each issue the same move closes; when the story stands in that state already, the same move sent again, each issue of it standing there too keeps it, so a comment that failed is written then; an issue's own move in the batch keeps its own reason or none. It holds at most 280 code points after trimming and no control, format, surrogate, unassigned or private-use character, no line or paragraph separator, and none of U+115F, U+2800 or U+3164, which show as blank; it is refused (MoveNotAllowed, whose own `reason` parameter is the planner's words, not this text) on a move into a state that is not closed, on an issue move whose issue stands in that state already, and on a store that keeps no reasons, before anything is written.

Moved.description: The board's revision after the save, every issue the batch moved, each once, and every run a confirmed save stopped.

stopped.description: Each run the save stopped; empty when it stopped none.

StoppedRun.description: A run a confirmed save of moves stopped, with each task at work the window must end.

StoppedTask.description: A task at work whose run a confirmed save of moves stopped, which the window ends.

Tracker.description: Where the planner keeps a project's stories and issues.

kind.description: `local` when the planner keeps them in a directory of this computer, which the person may choose; `github` when GitHub's tracker keeps them, as the mock mode answers too; `git` when the Git store keeps them as Markdown files in the project's repository.

items.description: Present only for `local`: the directory the planner uses, the default included. It is named absolute, unlike a path in a refusal's reason, since it is the person's own choice, shown to them and offered as where a folder dialog opens, and the answer goes only over loopback to a signed request. A kept or default directory that is no ItemsDirectory is never answered here: the project's reads are refused as ItemsDirectoryRefused instead.

default.description: Present only for `local`: the project's default directory, which `items` equals while no other directory is kept and which a PUT of `null` goes back to; a window offers going back to it only while `items` differs.

ItemsDirectoryRequest.description: The directory a local project's stories and issues are kept in, with the versions seen; it has no target. No other member is taken, and no member twice.

directory.description: The directory, or an explicit null for the default directory.

ItemsDirectory.description: A directory of this computer as an absolute path in normal form, the same rule for the planner and the window: at most 4095 bytes in UTF-8; no `.` or `..` segment, no empty segment such as `//`, and no trailing separator, the root alone excepted; no C0 or C1 control character (U+0000 to U+001F, U+007F to U+009F, U+0085 among them), no U+2028 or U+2029, no bidirectional control (U+202A to U+202E, U+2066 to U+2069), and no unpaired surrogate; no white space at its start or end, which is refused, never trimmed. On Linux it starts with `/`. On Windows it is a drive path, a letter, `:` and `\`, with `\` as its only separator; a UNC or device path (`\\server\...`, `\\.\...`, `\\?\...`) is refused.

Worker.description: Who works an issue, an agent through the tasks the planner starts or a person by hand.

WorkerRequest.description: An issue's new worker, with the versions seen; its target is the issue. No other member is taken.

WorkerSaved.description: The board's revision after the save and the new versions of what it changed.

Priority.description: A story's priority, the highest first.

PriorityRequest.description: A story's new priority, with the versions seen; its target is the story. No other member is taken.

PrioritySaved.description: The board's revision after the save and the new versions of what it changed: the story and its issues, since a priority raised on a story raises its issues with it.

NewIssueRequest.description: An idea a person wrote, with the versions seen; its target is the story named, if one is. No other member is taken.

title.description: One line without control characters; the spaces around it are dropped. At most 256 characters, as an issue's head holds its title.

mustBeTrue.description: The paragraph the issue's file opens with.

worker.description: Who works the new issue; AGENT when it is left out.

task.description: The Porelo task that proposed the idea, named in the new issue's file under what must be true; left out when no task did. An empty or malformed name is refused, never taken as none.

priority.description: The new issue's priority; Medium when it is left out.

story.description: The story the new issue is hung into, last in its list; none when it is left out.

state.description: The requested initial state, or the workflow's first state when left out. The GitHub store checks the placement before creating anything and writes it in the create's single save; closed states are refused. Other stores create in the first state and then move, answering PartlySaved if that move fails.

confirm.description: Whether the warnings of the move to state are confirmed, as a batch of moves confirms them.

labels.description: The new issue's topic labels; none when left out. On GitHub they are written in the create's single save and the issue read back, as an edit's labels are.

IssueAdded.description: The new issue's id, the board's revision after the save and the new versions of the issue and its named story.

Idea.description: The idea format, as a discussion's task reports it and a new story carries it: one story and an issue in each repository it concerns, each repository named once. One line means no control character or line break (U+0000 to U+001F, U+007F to U+009F, U+2028, U+2029); the spaces around a title, gain or test are dropped, and lengths count code points.

IdeaStory.description: A new story's title, what a user gains, its test and its priority, saved in the project's own repository; its state is the one the request that carries it gives it: the workflow's first state for an idea, its issues' for a story over issues that stand.

gain.description: What a user gains, one line.

test.description: How a person sees it work, one line.

IdeaIssue.description: One issue of the idea, saved in the workflow's first state in its repository.

repository.description: One of the project's repositories, named by no other issue of the idea.

mustBeTrue.description: The paragraph the issue's file opens with; not blank.

worker.description: Who works the issue, as the person chose it.

StoryRequest.description: A new story with its issues, in the idea format, with the versions seen; it has no target. No other member is taken.

StoryFromIssuesRequest.description: A new story over issues that stand on the board, with the versions seen; its targets are the issues named, and on a retry the story the earlier attempt made. No other member is taken, and no new issue is made.

existing.description: The issues the story takes, in its order, each named once.

StoryAdded.description: The new story's id, its issues' ids - the new ones in the idea's order, or the existing ones in the order named - the board's revision after the save and the new versions of what it changed.

IssueFieldsRequest.description: An issue's fields to set, with the versions seen; its target is the issue. A member left out stays as it is, null clears it where the issue may be without it, and no other member is taken.

size.description: The issue's size, XS to XL; null clears it.

estimateMinutes.description: The issue's estimate in minutes; null clears it.

rank.description: The issue's order within its priority, the lowest first; null clears it.

StoryIssuesRequest.description: A story's whole issue list, in its order, with the versions seen; its targets are the story and every issue hung in or taken out. No other member is taken.

ListIssueRequest.description: An issue the board offers among its unlisted issues, by its tracker reference, with the versions seen; its target is the unlisted issue, by its own version. No other member is taken. A fixed alias or an id of the Git store's form names no such issue and is refused (EditNotAllowed, field issue) before the board is read.

BlockedByRequest.description: An issue's whole list of blockers, with the versions seen; its target is the issue. No other member is taken.

CommentRequest.description: A comment's text; no other member is taken.

text.description: The person's text, as they wrote it; not blank, at most 65536 characters.

IssueTextRequest.description: An issue's title and named parts to write, with the versions seen; its target is the issue. A member left out stays as it is, null removes a part where the issue may be without it, and no other member is taken.

title.description: One line without control characters; the spaces around it are dropped. At most 256 characters, as a forge takes an issue's title.

covers.description: The first paragraph, which says what the issue covers; one paragraph, never removed.

whyThisSize.description: The paragraph after the lead Why this size; one paragraph; null removes it.

whatMustBeTrue.description: What must be true, never removed: one paragraph is written after the lead What must be true, a text of several paragraphs as the section What must be true.

plan.description: The section Plan; null removes it.

acceptance.description: The section Acceptance; null removes it.

openQuestions.description: The section Open questions; null removes it.

toBeChecked.description: The section To be checked; null removes it.

findings.description: The section Findings; null removes it.

StoryTextRequest.description: A story's title and parts to write, with the versions seen; its target is the story. A member left out stays as it is, null removes a part, and no other member is taken.

title.description: One line without control characters; the spaces around it are dropped. At most 256 characters, as a forge takes an issue's title.

gain.description: The paragraph after the lead What a user gains; one paragraph; null removes it.

test.description: The paragraph after the lead The test; one paragraph; null removes it.

EditSaved.description: The board's revision after the save and the new versions of what it changed.

revision.description: The revision, or null for a tracked project that holds no board yet.

open.description: What is still open of the whole board: every issue it holds, in a story or not, whatever stories the filter answers.

next.description: The next page cursor, or null when the selection is complete.

OpenWork.description: What is still open of a story or a board. An issue is left to build while it stands neither in a closed state nor in the review state: of the states a work rule's work ends in that are neither working nor closed, the one latest in the workflow, where the last work ends. An earlier work's end, such as an analysis's, is left to build. An issue left to build is blocked while an issue it waits on stands on the board neither in a closed state nor in the review state; it then counts as blocked, not under its state.

states.description: Each state of the workflow, in workflow order, with the number of its issues that are not blocked; zero included. An issue in a state the workflow lacks is counted in no state, but in every other figure.

blocked.description: The issues left to build that an open issue blocks.

sizes.description: Each size of the issues left to build, XS to XL, only the sizes that occur.

unsized.description: The issues left to build without a size.

left.description: The issues left to build, the blocked ones included.

minutes.description: The sum of `minutesLeft` over the issues left to build that have it, or null when none has; the issues without it are counted in `unestimated`. Summed before rounding, so it may differ from the sum of the rounded `minutesLeft` by a fraction.

unestimated.description: The issues left to build without `minutesLeft`.

review.description: The issues in the review state, which wait for the person.

OpenCount.description: A state's or a size's name with its number of issues.

Story.description: One story as the board shows it. Two stories share an id only when each carries the warning IdTwice; neither is then worked, moved or edited, and a read of the story by that id answers NoSuchStory.

state.description: One of the workflow's states; with a warning about its state, a value the workflow does not know, which the board shows in a column of its own at its end named after the value, or empty when no state can be told for it (NoState).

closedAt.description: When the story was closed as done, the day its test passed; null while it is open or closed for another reason, or where its store keeps no such time.

size.description: The story's size, XS to XL, given when it was estimated, or null when it has none. It is the story's own, never added up from its issues' sizes.

link.description: The story's web page, or null when it has none.

work.description: The current recorded run, null without a record.

open.description: What is still open of the story's issues and their sub-issues, each counted once. Null when the board does not hold every issue the story's head names, or holds one of its ids twice, so nothing is told as if it did.

warnings.description: What the store could not read in the story, which the board shows beside it; empty when nothing. The story is never left out for it.

IssueList.description: Issues at one revision: a whole story's with next null, or a page of those in no story.

next.description: The next page cursor, or null when the selection is complete.

Issue.description: One issue on the board. Two issues share an id only when each carries the warning IdTwice; neither is then worked, moved or edited, and a read of the issue by that id answers NoSuchIssue.

state.description: One of the workflow's states; with a warning about its state, a value the workflow does not know, which the board shows in a column of its own at its end named after the value.

size.description: The issue's size, or null when it has none.

priority.description: The issue's priority, Highest to Lowest; absent when the store holds none, or one outside them, which the issue's warnings then name.

minutesLeft.description: For an issue left to build, the minutes expected of it less those its work took so far, never below zero; what it took is its Minutes field as the store holds it. Expected is its estimate; without one, the median minutes of the finished issues of its size in its repository; without those, that median over every repository; without those, the minutes the planning repository's velocity seed, stats/seed.csv, gives its size. Null when it is not left to build or nothing gives an expectation.

blockedBy.description: The issues of the board blocking it.

waitsOn.description: The issues blocking it that the board does not hold, such as those of a repository outside the project. No building work is offered for it while any of them, or any of its board blockers, is not done; analysis, estimation and every other work take it like any other. A board blocker is done once it stands in the review state or in a closed state, and holds again once it is back in rework; a wait outside the board is done only once its tracker closed it. Work already started goes on. Empty when there are none.

parent.description: The issue this one is a sub-issue of, or null.

link.description: The issue's web page, or null when it has none.

worker.description: Who works it. A head that names none is worked by an agent; a sub-issue is worked as its parent is.

rounds.description: Absent when no reading record is known.

needsYou.description: Whether the person must act on it: a run of this planner raised it, with the reason in attention. An issue a person works, or one with no run here, is never raised.

noRunHere.description: Whether an issue an agent works stands in a working state while no run of this planner works it or a story holding it now, with a task offered or started, and no run raised it, such as work started elsewhere, set by a commit or moved by hand beside a run that ended; it is shown, not raised.

attention.description: Why the person must act, the reason the run reported; NONE when needsYou is false. INVALID_FINDINGS says a reader's findings could not be read: its reading stops, readingStopped true, for Read again or Review anyway. FAILED and BLOCKED of a reader stop its reading the same way. PLACE_CHANGED says what was read where the issue's work waits, or another author's end, named another task or place than the one the run keeps: the kept place stands and nothing moved. REJECTED_WITHOUT_POINTS says the push where the issue's work waits was rejected with nothing open, so no rework can say what to change. REVIEW_ROUNDS_USED says points stand open there after as many reworks at that place as the issue's readings allowed. PLACE_UNREADABLE says what is open there could not be read, wholly or in part; nothing moved, and it is read again. START_REFUSED says Porelo refused to start the issue's offered task, which stays offered: the refusal stands under Needs you until a Start of it goes through. PLACE_CLOSED says the pull request there was closed unmerged; MERGED_OTHER_HEAD says it merged, landed or was approved at another head than the one a reviewer reviewed there, or with none reviewed. Under a reviewer's rule, work merged or landed at the head reviewed, or approved there with nothing open and nothing held, moves the issue on to its rule's done state, Review; only the person sets Finished or Rejected.

warnings.description: What the store could not read in the issue, which the board shows beside it; empty when nothing. The issue is never left out for it.

RepositoryWarning.description: What is wrong in one of the project's repositories itself, rather than in a story or an issue: for TopicLabels, its labels differ from the topic labels every repository of a project carries - documentation, security, tests, build, dependencies, performance and usability, each with its color and description - or it still carries one of GitHub's eight default labels. Its own labels, those of neither list, are no part of it. It holds back no item and no work.

kind.description: An open name of what is wrong; a window shows a kind it does not know with its repository alone. The known kind is TopicLabels.

missing.description: The topic labels the repository lacks, in the topic labels' order.

defaults.description: GitHub's default labels the repository still carries, in GitHub's order.

differing.description: The topic labels the repository carries with another color or description, in the topic labels' order.

correction.description: The change the store offers to set the repository right, a Labels with no choices, or null when it offers none.

LabelCall.description: One call a repository's Labels correction makes on its forge: Delete a default label, which also takes it off every issue of the repository that carries it, Create a missing topic label, or Update a topic label's color and description to the topic labels'.

color.description: The color it is written with, six lower-case hexadecimal digits; null for a Delete.

description.description: The description it is written with, at most 100 characters; null for a Delete.

ItemWarning.description: What a store could not read in a story or an issue it still shows. A warning about the item's state, parent, blockers, id, kind, worker or risk holds it back, and every issue under it at any depth: no work starts on them, no edit changes them or adds them to a story or as a blocker or takes them out, and no move names them. A warning about the state alone still lets the item move, since a move into a state of the workflow sets it right, and lets each issue under it move too; so does the correction a store offers for it.

kind.description: An open name of what is wrong; a window shows a kind it does not know as any other. Known kinds are StateOutsideWorkflow, NoState, NoPriority, IdTwice, ParentOutsideProject, BlockerOutsideProject, IssueOutsideProject, WrongParent, BodyNotSectioned, StoryOutsideOwnRepository, ParentInOtherRepository, BlockedByStory, ParentCircle, SubIssueOfSubIssue, PastOnePage, DependsOnUnplaced, UnknownWorker, UnknownRisk, StoryUnderIssue, AlsoNeedsNotOnBoard, BodyTooLong, UnknownSize, UnknownPriority, UnreadableNumber, IssueBehindStory, UnknownLabel. IssueBehindStory is a story's: its words name each of its issues that stands before the state its issues give it, such as an issue in Idea in a story being implemented; it holds nothing back. UnknownLabel is a local item's whose file names a label outside the topic labels, as a hand edit of the file may; the label is shown and kept, and it holds nothing back.

text.description: Words saying what is wrong, for a tooltip, shown as plain text. They are fixed but for the places a store names: where a store sets nothing right itself, they name where the item is kept, so the person sets it right by hand there. The Git store names each copy's file and repository for IdTwice, and the story's for IssueOutsideProject; a file's path is relative to its repository and may hold a person's words, so it is named without control, format, bidi or zero-width characters and capped at 200 characters with an ellipsis.

holds.description: Whether the planner holds back the item for this warning: no work starts on it, and neither an edit nor a move names it, but for a move out of a state the workflow does not know. Since kinds are open, a window tells by this field which warning holds an item.

correction.description: The one change the store offers to set the warning right, or null when it offers none: the store decides it when it reads the board, and offers none while another warning holds the item back or the work rules have faults. The Git store offers a Move for an issue's StateOutsideWorkflow alone; the GitHub store offers the same Move, and a Priority for a story's NoPriority and UnknownPriority with the priorities the organization's issue field Priority holds; none when the owner has no such field or it could not be read.

Correction.description: The one change that sets a warning right, which the person picks and confirms on the board.

kind.description: An open name of the change; a window offers a kind it does not know as none. Known kinds are Move - the issue moved into the state picked, previewed and saved through /moves/preview and /moves as any move of it -, Priority - the story's priority set to the one picked, previewed and saved through /corrections/preview and /corrections - and Labels - a repository's labels brought to the topic labels, previewed and saved through /corrections/preview and /corrections.

choices.description: What the person picks from, each a name a request sends back as its `choice`; a state whose name is none such is not offered. At least one for every kind but a Labels, which offers none and has it empty. For a Move, the states in the workflow's order: its open states that no work alone enters, so a correction neither closes the item nor starts work on it. They are what the window offers: a Move is judged as any move by /moves, which may move the issue into any state of the workflow, a closed one too. For a Priority, the priorities the store can hold, the highest first, each one of Highest, High, Medium, Low and Lowest.

CorrectionRequest.description: The correction of one warning on one story, issue or repository, with what the person picked, previewed against the board as the planner reads it; it names exactly one story, one issue or one repository and carries no versions.

warning.description: The kind of the warning it sets right.

choice.description: What the person picked among the correction's `choices`: a state's name for a Move, a priority for a Priority; left out for a Labels, which offers none. The planner checks it against the choices it offers and refuses any other, and a missing one, (CorrectionRefused).

CorrectionConfirm.description: A correction the person confirmed, with the digest of its preview and the versions seen, its preview's targets; it names exactly one story, one issue or one repository. A repository's has no targets and sends `seen` as exactly `{}`.

choice.description: What the person picked, as its preview was asked with; left out for a Labels.

CorrectionPreview.description: What a correction would write, and the digest its save sends back.

targets.description: Every item the correction changes, each once with the version it stands at. The save sends them back in `seen`. Empty for a Labels, which changes no item.

story.description: The story it writes, or null.

issue.description: The issue it writes, or null.

repository.description: The repository whose labels it writes, or null.

warning.description: The kind of the warning it sets right.

from.description: What the item holds now of what the correction changes, empty when none is told; a Priority's warning tells none, so it is empty for one, and so is a Labels', whose calls say what changes.

to.description: What it is written with, the choice picked; empty for a Labels, which its calls say.

calls.description: For a Labels, every call it makes on the repository's forge, in the order it makes them: each default label deleted, then each missing topic label created, then each differing one updated, each in its list's order; the repository's own labels are never named. Empty for every other kind.

CorrectionSaved.description: The board's revision and the versions of the corrected targets after the save; a correction never writes a state, so it stops no run.

HeldIssue.description: An open issue of the story no task of the proposal names, since the board holds it back. A warning holds it back from every work; a blocker or a wait not done only from the building work, the one that builds and pushes and takes work from the backlog state, so analysis, estimation and every other work take it.

reason.description: Why, in the words of its warnings, of its id that names two issues, of the blockers it waits on, or of a held parent above it, named as "it stands under" the parent followed by the parent's own reason.

Wait.description: An issue an issue of the board waits on that the board does not hold.

reference.description: The issue as owner/repository#number, or null when the tracker names a blocker the person's login cannot read.

done.description: Whether it is done; null when it could not be read, which holds the issue back as not done.

link.description: Where a person reads it on the tracker, or null when not known.

IssueDetail.description: One issue with its text and sub-issues.

whatMustBeTrue.description: The issue's What must be true paragraph; absent when the text has none.

to.description: A state named by the workflow.

ChosenIssues.description: The story's issues the work is for, each an open issue of the story an agent works, standing in a state the target's rule takes work from, or in the target itself where the story's run raised it with the reason the Start passes over, or for a proposal with any reason a Start may pass over, and it is worked there again; absent for the story's own work, its least advanced open issues the rule takes from. A list naming any other issue is refused whole.

coordinator.description: START until the run supplies an active coordinator record; otherwise TELL.

manual.description: The story's open issues a person works (worker MANUAL), in story order: no task of this proposal names them, and a person moves them through the work by hand.

held.description: The story's open issues held back, in story order, each with why: by a warning about their state, parent, blockers or id, or, for the building work alone, by an open blocker or wait. No task of this proposal names them. A Start naming one is refused.

issues.description: The proposal's issue identities in order; immutable at acceptance.

role.description: The role the work rule offers this task, as the project's work rules define it: one that pushes work for work that builds; one that reports findings for a reading started by hand, which starts one task per issue reading the issue's last landed build, with no helpers. The planner's words: of a role sent back only the name is read, and it must be the offered one.

brief.description: The rule's order, expanded after the operator's final choices.

effort.description: The effort chosen: the rule's for the issues' risk as proposed, or the person's as sent back; null for none. An open name, not an enum, since its values are Porelo's per agent.

chosenBy.description: Where the rule's choice of agent, model and effort came from, for example "Reading, risk harm"; the planner's words, which it never takes back from a caller. Empty when not known.

offered.description: Every agent the rule offers this task, each with the model it offers, in the rule's order, the proposed agent first, so a window can preselect the first one ready on the machine the task goes to. The planner's words, which it never takes back from a caller; absent where it names none, as in a run's record or from an older planner.

kind.description: The helper's kind inside its main task, the planner's own word; a helper is no task and has no role.

choice.description: KEEP starts the helper as proposed, with the proposed effort whether it is sent back or not, and refuses another; CHANGE takes the agent, model and effort sent back.

effort.description: The effort chosen: the rule's for the issues' risk as proposed, or the person's as sent back; null for none. An open name, not an enum, since its values are Porelo's per agent.

chosenBy.description: Where the rule's choice of agent, model and effort came from, for example "Reading, risk harm"; the planner's words, which it never takes back from a caller. Empty when not known.

issueReadingRounds.description: Only proposal issues, each at most once.

PassOver.description: The reason of one issue a Start answers with a new run in place of the run named, as the person saw it.

StopRequest.description: The run the person saw, which the stop ends only while it stands.

idea.description: The person's first words of the idea, not blank, counted in Unicode code points.

PlanningStartTask.description: One task for Porelo's Start. The members `readOnly`, `allRepositories`, `noGate`, `place`, `rights`, `readLanded`, `writeAs` and `projectServices` are named as Start takes them and are handed to it as given: the window derives none of them and adds none. The order has no other member for Start's parts, and none for `credentials`, `clearance` or `upstream`, which the planner never hands on. No member names the kind of the workspace: `readOnly` (with `allRepositories` where every repository is read) is read only, `noGate` is no workspace, a `place` at another task's push or pull request is that task's work, and anything else is the task's own work. repository and role are present for work and absent for a discussion; result is present only for a task whose role hands back a result, and given only for it.

kind.description: work for a task a work rule offers, which names its role; discussion for the task that discusses an idea with the person, which names none.

role.description: The role bound to the offer, as the project's work rules define it, for the person to read; Start is handed no role. Present for work, absent for a discussion.

task.description: The name of the existing Porelo task Start is to run again, handed to Start as its task as given: present exactly for an author sent back to its own work, at its task's gate push or at its task's own pull request, and absent for every new task. Never present where the place is another task's work.

ownTask.description: Present only as true: Start is asked under a task name of the window's own choosing, one no task of the project holds, never the repository's own task. Set for a task that reads another task's work and for the building work of an issue the run's Start held back; absent for every other. Never present together with `task`.

opensTerminal.description: Present only as true, on at most one task of an answer: the first task with mode AGENT whose role pushes work, or a discussion's own task. The window opens its terminal on that task; when none qualifies, none is marked.

effort.description: The effort Start is handed: the one the person's order sent back for a task started by hand, the rule's for the issues' risk for one that starts by itself; absent for none.

chosenBy.description: Where the rule's choice of agent, model and effort came from; absent when not known.

prompt.description: The complete starting prompt, at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes.

result.description: The plain name of the file the task hands back, without a directory: analysis.json, estimate.json or readiness.json for a stage that hands back its result.

given.description: The files the task is given to read, read only, in the order of its issues: each issue's text as the store holds it now, newer than any copy in the task's checkout. Absent or empty for work that pushes. At most 16 files, each text at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes, all together at most 1048576.

readOnly.description: Start's `readOnly`, present only as true, for a task that only reads.

allRepositories.description: Start's `allRepositories`, present only as true, for a task that reads every repository of the project.

noGate.description: Start's `noGate`, present only as true, for a task without a workspace.

rights.description: Start's `rights`, always named and never left to Porelo's default: the actions and judgments of the task's role in one list. An empty list is a task holding no right.

readLanded.description: Start's `readLanded`, always named: the Porelo task names whose forwarded work the task also reads, so Porelo's gate gives it their branches read only; empty for none.

projectServices.description: Start's `projectServices`, always named: whether the task has the project's services; always false for a task at another task's work.

writeAs.description: Start's `writeAs`, the account the task's released words are written as; present only where the place is a pull request, since Start refuses it anywhere else.

work.description: What Start is handed to name the tracker's issue the task works and its stage; present only on a planned stage's task of a project a tracker keeps, never on a discussion's, and absent, never null, otherwise.

place.description: Where the run works, handed to Start as its `place` unchanged; absent only for a new task's own gate push, which Start takes as the default. A task at another task's work always names its place, the one push or pull request it reads, which alone tells Start whose work it is. The gate push of a task sent back to its own work is that task's own, and the order's `task` names it.

RunPlace.description: Where a run works. Exactly one member is present.

pullRequest.description: A pull request at the forge by its https address, such as https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/12: ASCII only, with a host and without user info, query or fragment; Porelo judges at Start which forge the host names.

ownPullRequest.description: The task's own pull request, the one its pushes opened; present only as true.

GatePush.description: A push waiting at Porelo's gate, named by its task's name within the project.

repository.description: The project's repository; absent for the task's own.

issue.description: The tracker's issue with its owner, `<owner>/<repository>#<number>`: one line without white space and without `..`, at most 200 characters.

phase.description: The name of the stage's phase the task works, one line that is not blank, at most 64 characters.

name.description: The plain file name, an issue's id the task owns with .md; a tracker reference's `#` is written as `-` (`porelo-planner-12.md` for `porelo-planner#12`), so no file name Porelo mounts holds a `#`.

text.description: The issue's text, at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes.

Right.description: One of Porelo's fixed words for what a task may do, as its Start takes them: the actions at its place (push, reply, openThreads, resolveThreads), the rights of its own endpoint (start, stop, done, report) and the one judgment, reject. What each allows is Porelo's to say.

WriteAs.description: The account a task's released words are written as at a pull request, in Porelo's words: author, the account that opened it, or review, the forge's account for reviews.

TaskRole.description: A role of the project's tasks, as its work rules define it: a name, how its task ends and the parts of a start. The planner knows no role by its name, so a role a project adds is served like any other; Porelo is never handed a role, only the parts.

name.description: The role's name in the project's work rules, shown as given; the work rules load no name that holds a control character or a format character, such as one that changes the direction of text.

endKind.description: How a task of the role ends, from the planner's fixed list: it pushes work, reports findings, gives points at a place, or hands back a result. A role that may reject ends as GIVES_POINTS and holds reject among its rights.

workspace.description: The kind of the role's workspace, in the words Porelo's task row records it by: the task's own work, another task's work, read only for one repository or for all, or no workspace. Shown only; a start order tells the workspace by Start's own members.

readLanded.description: Whether a task of the role also reads the forwarded work of the tasks whose build it reads.

projectServices.description: Whether a task of the role has the project's services; never true for another task's work.

rights.description: The role's actions and judgments in one list; empty for a role holding no right.

RefName.description: A Git ref name of 1 to 255 characters (Unicode code points), letters beyond ASCII included, without "..", control characters, spaces, line or paragraph separators or any of ~^:?*[\, not starting with - or /, not ending with / or .lock.

Landing.description: Where a task's work landed, copied unchanged from Porelo's task row; the planner never derives one of these names. A reader's order names the commit and the remote-tracking name, read after `git fetch origin`.

ref.description: The ref Porelo serves the work under, a RefName starting with refs/.

remote.description: The remote-tracking name a reader sees after a plain git fetch, such as origin/landed/t/b.

commit.description: The landed commit, 40 or 64 lowercase hex digits.

machine.description: The machine's name as the person sees it, 1 to 128 Unicode code points (not UTF-16 code units), without control characters or line breaks. Kept and answered back verbatim, never used as a path, a file name or a URL.

TaskEventRequest.description: container is required for every event but REFUSED and forbidden for it, since Porelo started none; ended is required only for ENDED and forbidden for the others; landed, with at least one entry, is required only for LANDED and forbidden for the others, whose end carries its own; refusal is required only for REFUSED and forbidden for the others.

TaskRefusal.description: What Porelo refused a Start with, kept as given; the planner judges no name.

name.description: Porelo's name for the refusal, 1 to 64 letters and digits.

parameters.description: The refusal's parameters, each key 1 to 64 characters; no control character anywhere.

detail.description: Porelo's words, possibly empty, with no control character but line breaks.

answer.description: The agent's unmapped answer, at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes.

landed.description: Where the task's work landed, copied unchanged from Porelo's task row; absent or empty while the work still waits at the gate.

outcome.description: The outcome the task declared, copied unchanged from Porelo's end record; absent when it declared none. BLOCKED and FAILED leave the task's issues in their state under Needs you, whatever finished says, and why carries the task's reason; DONE and an absent outcome are judged by finished and unpushed, and the end of a task whose role reports findings by finished and its findings alone, since it delivers only its answer.

mode.description: The rework's mode, one of the Reworking rule's modes. mode, agent and model come together or not at all; without them a rework takes the rule's first mode and first model, and another choice refuses them as InvalidSettings.

agent.description: The rework's agent, one of the Reworking rule's agents.

model.description: The rework's model, the Reworking rule's model for that agent.

StageResultRequest.description: A stage task's offer and either the result file it wrote, handed on unchanged, or one line why it left none; exactly one of result and missing, and no other member.

offer.description: The offer of the stage's task, as the planner offered it.

missing.description: One line why the task left no result: no file, one too large or one unreadable. Length in code points.

StageResultFile.description: The result format porelo-stage-result-1, as the task wrote it to analysis.json, estimate.json or readiness.json, within a hand-in of at most 1052672 bytes including its envelope: one entry per issue the order named. ANALYSIS needs plan, size and sizeWhy and takes no estimateMinutes; ESTIMATE needs size, sizeWhy and estimateMinutes, and plan corrects the plan; neither takes ready, lacks or why. READINESS needs ready and takes nothing else for a ready issue, and lacks and why for an issue not ready, never a member of the other kinds. No text holds a control or direction character, but a plan its newlines; lengths are in code points. Unknown members are refused, so a later format changes format.

StageResultIssue.description: One issue's entry. size and sizeWhy are required of ANALYSIS and ESTIMATE, ready of READINESS.

plan.description: Markdown, the base design read in today's code.

ready.description: Whether the issue names a plan, a size and its blockers, or that it has none.

lacks.description: What an issue not ready lacks.

why.description: One line why the issue is not ready, kept beside it.

StageResultReply.description: The offer's outcome - SAVED, its issues moved to the rule's done state, those a readiness check found not ready back to the rule's from state, or MISSING, its issues left where they stand - and the offer's issues as the board shows them now.

starts.description: The run's offers made without a request of the window's, which wait for their Start: an author sent back to answer the points open at the gate push its work waits at, with the role that built the work and that push as its place, started under that push's name; an author sent back to answer the points open at its task's own pull request, once Porelo forwarded the gate push there, with the same role and place ownPullRequest, started under the same task's name; or, where the reading rule names a role that reads another task's work, a task of that role at a new head at the place the work waits at, with that place, started under a task name of its own, never the name of the task whose work it reads; or the building work of an issue the run's Start held back by a blocker or a wait not done, once each of them stands in review or closed, with the building rule's role, no place and no result, for that one issue, which the run's repositories then list, started under a task name of its own, and served only while nothing holds the issue back on the board as it stands. The window starts each once, through the callback it gives for offers it did not ask for; empty when none waits, and for a stopped or halted run.

machine.description: The machine's name as the person sees it, kept and answered back verbatim, never used as a path, a file name or a URL. Null until a report names it. Length is measured in Unicode code points, not UTF-16 code units.

effort.description: The effort the task's order said it starts with, as the person's order sent it back; null when nobody said, as for a task that started by itself, never the offered effort.

role.description: The role the task was started with, as the project's work rules defined it then.

readLanded.description: The Porelo task names whose forwarded work the task was started to read besides; empty for none.

place.description: Where the run works, as the offer the task was bound to handed it to Start. Absent for a new task's own gate push, which Start takes as the default. A pull request is an address from outside, to be shown as plain text and never opened by itself.

held.description: How many undecided held items Porelo's newest record of this task gives, as that record was read since the planner started. Absent when it is unknown: no record of the task was read, or Porelo's record gives no count because the task's hold journal cannot be read or the record predates the count. Absent is shown as unknown, never as 0; the number is shown as served and nothing is judged from it.

reason.description: Why the issue needs attention, NONE if it does not; MANUAL says a person now works it by hand, so no further task of the run takes it, no role is bound to it and it needs nobody's attention; it is shown as the person's. BLOCKING_FINDINGS and ROUND_LIMIT both stop a reading with blocking findings, readingStopped true: below the readings granted and at them. INVALID_FINDINGS stops a reading whose findings could not be read, readingStopped true, with a round counted, roundsMost raised by one without using up the limit, and no findings kept: the person has the same build read again or takes it to Review; an issue moved meanwhile gets NEXT_STEP_UNAVAILABLE without a stop, as at any end. FAILED says the task did not finish or declared its work failed, BLOCKED that it declared its work blocked; the issue stays in its state and the task's why says what went wrong. A reader's FAILED or BLOCKED stops its reading as INVALID_FINDINGS does, readingStopped true, with a round counted, roundsMost raised by one without using up the limit, and no findings kept. PLACE_CHANGED says what was read where the issue's work waits, or another author's end, named another task or place than the run keeps, or that Porelo refused to start the issue's rework at its kept place as NotTheTasksPush; the kept place stands and nothing moved. START_REFUSED says Porelo refused to start the issue's offered task, with `startRefusal` naming why; the offer stays offered and nothing moved. REJECTED_WITHOUT_POINTS, REVIEW_ROUNDS_USED, PLACE_UNREADABLE, PLACE_CLOSED and MERGED_OTHER_HEAD stop an issue whose work waits at a place: rejected with nothing open, its reworks there used up, what is open there unreadable, closed unmerged, or merged, landed or approved at another head than the one reviewed; nothing moved. Points or findings open there, with nothing held and no task of the issue offered or at work, send the issue back to its rework instead, its author offered again in starts; a reviewer offered there and not started yet holds the rework back, and an end read there voids that reviewer. A move of the issue by hand clears its reason and its stop.

startRefusal.description: What Porelo refused the Start of the issue's offered task with, present while that refusal stands, the reason being START_REFUSED, or PLACE_CHANGED for a rework refused as NotTheTasksPush. A StartRuleBroken names its `rule` and `detail` in the refusal's parameters as Porelo gave them, and a RightsChanged names nothing.

file.description: A display-only relative label, without a leading slash or backslash or any parent segment.

Problem.description: A refusal; the last part of its type is the refusal's name.

detail.description: The planner's words for the refusal, never a credential or a local path.

parameters.description: Typed subjects and checked words describing the refusal; only the members the refusal names are present, never one written as null.

branch.description: The branch of the source a SaveFromElsewhere refusal names, when it named one.

save.description: The held save a resend or a drop is refused for.

address.description: A forge's https origin, for NoForgeAccess.

right.description: The right a forge names as missing, for NoForgeAccess, when it names one.

directory.description: The directory an ItemsDirectoryRefused refusal names, absolute: the person's own choice, named to them over loopback to a signed request, unlike a path in a refusal's reason.

changed.description: The targets an ItemChanged refusal names, each once.

items.description: Each target an ItemChanged refusal names, as the store holds it now or gone.

missing.description: The targets a BasisIncomplete refusal names, for which `seen` holds no version.

field.description: The member of a new issue's or an edit's body a refusal is about, or empty.

issues.description: Comma-joined, each issue with its state.

faults.description: An idea's or a stage result's faults, each starting with the field it names, in fixed words.

part.description: The text part a refused text write is about, by its heading as the text writes it (What must be true, Plan), or `title`; empty when the write names no one part.

fault.description: What is wrong in the part a refused text write names.

found.description: The line of the part that holds the fault, at most its first 200 characters; empty for LENGTH and SECTIONS.

key.description: The key of a new issue of a board change a KeyRefused or NoSuchKey refusal names.

Outline.description: The board in short, as getOutline answers it.

issues.description: The issues no story names that are not sub-issues of an issue a story names.

next.description: The next page cursor, or null when the selection is complete.

OutlineIssue.description: One issue in short; size and priority are null where the board shows none.

TextParts.description: An issue's text by its parts, each by the name setIssueText writes it under; a part the text does not hold is absent.

IssueParts.description: One issue with its fields and its text by parts.

story.description: The story that names the issue, or null when none does.

parts.description: The text's parts, or null when its sections cannot be told apart for certain.

text.description: The whole text, given only when its parts are null.

fault.description: The first thing to repair, given only when the parts are null.

Breaches.description: The breaches of the stories' rules at a revision.

Breach.description: One breach of a stories' rule, with the story it concerns and the issues it names.

story.description: The story the breach concerns, or null for an issue in no story.

SearchAnswer.description: The items whose title or text holds every word searched for.

next.description: The next page cursor, or null when the selection is complete.

SearchMatch.description: One matching story or issue and where its words were found.

found.description: Where the words were found, `title`, a part's name or `text` (a text that cannot be split, or words outside every part), each once.

StateMoves.description: Issues each moved to a state.

StateMove.description: One issue moved to a state, each issue once in a batch.

reason.description: Why the issue is closed, taken only on a move into a closed state, as Move's reason; with through, it goes with the last step.

through.description: The states the issue passes before its target, in order, each judged and saved as a move of its own on the board the steps before it leave, so the issue's history shows each stage. A step the rules refuse refuses the whole move with that step named (its from and to), and nothing of it is saved; a store failure after a step stood answers the issue PartlySaved, naming the steps that stand. No closed state is passed, none twice, and neither the issue's own state nor its target.

BoardChange.description: New issues and changes of existing issues, applied in one call.

ItemKey.description: A key of the caller's naming a new issue inside one body.

ItemRef.description: An existing issue's or story's id, or the key of a new issue of the same body.

NewItem.description: One new issue, written into the workflow's first state unless `state` names another.

parts.description: The text by parts; whatMustBeTrue is required.

ItemUpdate.description: Changes of one existing issue; a member left out stays as it is, a part null is removed as setIssueText removes it, and blockedBy is the whole new list.

estimateMinutes.description: The issue's estimate in minutes, written beside its size as setIssueFields writes it; null clears it. A store that keeps no estimate refuses the update as setIssueFields does.

through.description: Taken only beside state: the states the issue passes before its target, in order, each judged and saved as a move of its own on the board the steps before it leave, so the issue's history shows each stage. A step the rules refuse refuses the whole move with that step named (its from and to), and no step of it is saved, while the update's other members written before it stand and answer PartlySaved; a store failure after a step stood answers the issue PartlySaved, naming the steps that stand. No closed state is passed, none twice, and neither the issue's own state nor its target.

ManyFields.description: Fields of many issues and priorities of stories, set in one save.

IssueFieldsSet.description: One issue's fields to set; a member left out stays as it is, and at least one is named.

BatchSaved.description: What a batch saved and refused, per item, the revision after it and the new versions of what it changed.

ItemResult.description: One item of a batch: SAVED when its change stands, UNCHANGED when it asked for what stood already, REFUSED with the refusal as the call alone would have answered it.

item.description: The item's id; for a new issue, its id when it stands, otherwise null.

key.description: A new issue's key, as sent.

state.description: A moved issue's state after the batch.

version.description: The item's known version after the batch, for a SAVED or UNCHANGED item the read-back holds as one item; absent for a REFUSED item or when its new version could not be read.

raised.description: For a story's priority, the issues raised with it.
